articles.title: Direction of a lattice dart
articles.statement: The direction `head - tail` of a dart, one of the four unit vectors of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: Base boundary dart of the domino
articles.statement: The boundary dart `dmD0` of the domino, as an element of the subtype of boundary darts.

articles.title: Downward domino dart at the left site
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the domino from `(0, 0)` downwards.

articles.title: Leftward domino dart at the left site
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the domino from `(0, 0)` to the left.

articles.title: Upward domino dart at the left site
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the domino from `(0, 0)` upwards.

articles.title: Upward domino dart at the right site
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the domino from `(1, 0)` upwards.

articles.title: Rightward domino dart at the right site
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the domino from `(1, 0)` to the right.

articles.title: Downward domino dart at the right site
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the domino from `(1, 0)` downwards.

articles.title: Face loop around the domino
articles.statement: The closed walk of faces around the domino, of length six.

articles.title: Domino as a two-site set
articles.statement: The two-site set `{(0, 0), (1, 0)}`.

articles.title: Dart correspondence respects reversal
articles.statement: Reversing a lattice dart corresponds to `SimpleGraph.Dart.symm`.

articles.title: Lattice darts agree with graph darts of the square lattice
articles.statement: Lattice darts are exactly Mathlib's darts of the square lattice.

articles.title: Boundary degree of a unit face
articles.statement:
The number of the four edges of the unit face at `(a, b)` that have exactly one
endpoint
in `S`.

articles.title: Lower left corner of the unit face at $(a, b)$
articles.statement: The lower left corner `(a, b)` of the unit face `[a, a + 1] × [b, b + 1]`.

articles.title: Upper left corner of the unit face at $(a, b)$
articles.statement: The upper left corner `(a, b + 1)` of the unit face `[a, a + 1] × [b, b + 1]`.

articles.title: Lower right corner of the unit face at $(a, b)$
articles.statement: The lower right corner `(a + 1, b)` of the unit face `[a, a + 1] × [b, b + 1]`.

articles.title: Upper right corner of the unit face at $(a, b)$
articles.statement: The upper right corner `(a + 1, b + 1)` of the unit face `[a, a + 1] × [b, b + 1]`.

articles.title: Total turning over the minimal period is divisible by four
articles.statement:
The total signed turning around a boundary orbit, taken over its minimal period, is divisible by
 `4`.

articles.title: Total turning of a closed orbit segment is divisible by four
articles.statement:
If the orbit of `e` closes after `p` steps, the total signed turning over these steps is
 divisible by `4`.

articles.title: Boundary darts with heads in one component share an orbit
articles.statement:
Boundary darts of `K` whose heads lie in the same connected component of `Kᶜ` lie in the same
boundary orbit.

articles.title: Boundary dart of a set of sites
articles.statement: `e` is a boundary dart of `K`: it points from a site of `K` to a site outside `K`.

articles.title: Inner corner of a boundary dart
articles.statement:
The site `e.head + r`, with `r` the clockwise rotation of `e.dir`, lies in `K`; then the
successor of `e` has the same head.

articles.title: Iterates up to the minimal period are distinct
articles.statement:
The iterates `f^[j] x` for `1 ≤ j ≤ minimalPeriod f x` are distinct. See also Mathlib's
`Function.iterate_injOn_Iio_minimalPeriod`, the same statement for `0 ≤ j < minimalPeriod f x`.

articles.title: King adjacency on the square lattice
articles.statement: King adjacency on `ℤ²`: distinct sites that differ by at most one in each coordinate.

articles.title: Number of convex corners in a boundary orbit
articles.statement:
The number of steps `i < p` in the boundary orbit of `e` with turn `turnZ = -1` (convex
corners of `K`).

articles.title: Dart from a site in a unit direction
articles.statement: The dart from `p` to `p + g`, for a unit vector `g`.

articles.title: Face loop left of one period of a boundary orbit
articles.statement: The closed walk of faces to the left of the darts in one period of the boundary orbit of `a`.

articles.title: Minimal-period orbit loop as a lattice walk
articles.statement: The closed face walk of one period of the orbit of `a`, as a walk in the square lattice.

articles.title: Closure under the diagonal fill rules
articles.statement: `S` is closed under the two diagonal fill rules of `StatMech.Lattice.ndt_StarHullMem`.

articles.title: Product set of two coordinate sets in the plane
articles.statement: The product set `{x | x 0 ∈ A ∧ x 1 ∈ B}`.

articles.title: Membership in the star hull
articles.statement:
Membership in the star hull of `K`: sites of `K`, closed under filling the lower right corner
of a face whose lower left and upper right corners are members, and the lower left corner of
a face whose lower right and upper left corners are members.

articles.title: Star hull of a set of lattice sites
articles.statement: The star hull of `K`: the smallest superset of `K` closed under the diagonal fill rules.

articles.title: Sublevel set of a separable function
articles.statement: The sublevel set `{x | φ (x 0) + ψ (x 1) ≤ c}` of a separable function.

articles.title: Diagonal touch at a face
articles.statement: `K` contains exactly two opposite corners of the face `f`.

articles.title: No diagonal touch along a boundary orbit
articles.statement: No face visited in one period of the orbit of `a` is a diagonal touch of `K`.

articles.title: Set with no diagonal touches
articles.statement: `K` has no diagonal touch at any face.

articles.title: Lower left corner of a face $f$
articles.statement: The lower left corner of the face `f`. This is `StatMech.Lattice.faceCorner00 (f 0) (f 1)`.

articles.title: Upper left corner of a face $f$
articles.statement: The upper left corner of the face `f`.

articles.title: Lower right corner of a face $f$
articles.statement: The lower right corner of the face `f`.

articles.title: Upper right corner of a face $f$
articles.statement: The upper right corner of the face `f`.

articles.title: King-saturated set
articles.statement:
Whenever `K` contains two opposite corners of a face, it contains one of the other two
corners.

articles.title: Boundary orbit face loop as a lattice walk
articles.statement: The face loop of the boundary orbit of `e`, as a closed walk in the square lattice.

articles.title: No-pinch condition for a boundary orbit
articles.statement: Darts in one period of the orbit of `a` that have the same face also have the same direction.

articles.title: Orbit saturation by heads connected in the complement
articles.statement:
Boundary darts whose heads are connected in `Kᶜ` lie in the same orbit; a reformulation of
`StatMech.Lattice.InterfaceConnected`.

articles.title: Boundary orbits spread along king moves
articles.statement:
If the orbit of `e` reaches a site outside `K`, it reaches every king neighbour of that site
outside `K`.

articles.title: Boundary orbit with a full revolution has length at least four
articles.statement: A boundary orbit that makes a full revolution has length at least `4`.

articles.title: Site reached by a boundary orbit
articles.statement: Some boundary dart in the orbit of `e` has head `v`.

articles.title: Orbit saturation at reached sites
articles.statement: Every boundary dart whose head is reached by the orbit of `e` lies in that orbit.

articles.title: Walk along the first iterates of a boundary dart
articles.statement: The walk `a, next a, …, next^[n] a` in `dartSuccGraph K`.

articles.title: Reversal of a lattice dart
articles.statement: The dart with tail and head exchanged.

articles.title: Number of reflex corners in a boundary orbit
articles.statement:
The number of steps `i < p` in the boundary orbit of `e` with turn `turnZ = 1` (reflex
corners of `K`).

articles.title: Four quarter turns of the square lattice are the identity
articles.statement:
Four counterclockwise quarter turns are the identity, i.e. every site is a periodic point of
 `rot90Fun` of period `4`.

articles.title: Quarter-turn rotations form an action of $\mathbb{Z}/4$
articles.statement: `rotPow` is an action of the additive group `ZMod 4`.

articles.title: Nontrivial quarter-turn rotations fix no lattice direction
articles.statement:
A nontrivial rotation moves every lattice direction: `rotPow s` fixes the direction of a dart
 only for `s = 0`.

articles.title: Rotation of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ by a number of quarter turns
articles.statement: Rotation of `ℤ²` by `s` counterclockwise quarter turns, `s : ZMod 4`.

articles.title: Two darts in the same boundary orbit
articles.statement: The dart `f` is obtained from `e` by iterating the boundary successor map of `K`.

articles.title: Corner balance of a simple lattice polygon
articles.statement:
The numbers of reflex and convex corners along the orbit of `a` differ by `4` or `-4`, the
corner count of a simple lattice polygon.

articles.title: Number of straight steps in a boundary orbit
articles.statement: The number of steps `i < p` in the boundary orbit of `e` with turn `0`.

articles.title: Total signed turning along a boundary orbit
articles.statement:
The total signed turning (in quarter turns) over the first `p` steps of the `dartNext K`-orbit
 of `e`.

articles.title: Signed quarter turn between consecutive boundary darts
articles.statement:
The signed quarter turn from `e` to `dartNext K e`: `1` counterclockwise, `0` straight, `-1`
 clockwise. Its reduction mod `4` is `turn K e`.

articles.title: Quarter turn between consecutive boundary darts modulo 4
articles.statement:
The quarter turn, as an element of `ZMod 4`, from the boundary dart `e` of `K` to its successor
 `dartNext K e`: `1` for a counterclockwise (left) turn, `0` for going straight, `3` for a
 clockwise (right) turn.

articles.title: Boundary orbit making exactly one full revolution
articles.statement:
The boundary orbit through `a` turns by exactly one full revolution, i.e. its total signed
 turning is `4` or `-4` quarter turns.

articles.title: Base boundary dart of the unit cell
articles.statement: The rightward boundary dart of the unit cell, as an element of the subtype of boundary darts.

articles.title: Rightward boundary dart of the unit cell
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the unit cell pointing right.

articles.title: Downward boundary dart of the unit cell
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the unit cell pointing down.

articles.title: Leftward boundary dart of the unit cell
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the unit cell pointing left.

articles.title: Upward boundary dart of the unit cell
articles.statement: The boundary dart of the unit cell pointing up.

articles.title: Face loop around the unit cell
articles.statement: The closed walk of faces around the unit cell, of length four.

articles.title: Unit cell as a one-site set
articles.statement: The one-site set `{(0, 0)}`.

articles.title: $\ell^1$ norm of a vector in $\mathbb{Z}^2$
articles.statement: The `ℓ¹` norm `|z 0| + |z 1|` of a vector of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: Each face visited once per period by a boundary orbit
articles.statement: Every face visited by the orbit of `a` is visited exactly once per period.

articles.title: Four unit vectors of $\mathbb{Z}^2$
articles.statement: The four unit vectors of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: Local turn of a boundary orbit at a face
articles.statement: The sum of the turns `turnZ` at the visits of the orbit of `a` to the face `f`.

articles.title: Faces visited by a boundary orbit in one period
articles.statement: The set of faces visited in one period of the orbit of `a`.

articles.title: $p_c(\mathbb{Z}^2) < 1$ under a no-pinch hypothesis
articles.statement:
`p_c(ℤ²) < 1`, under the hypothesis that for every configuration with a finite origin cluster
the boundary orbit of the exit dart has period at least three, has no pinch, and contains the
left exit dart.

articles.title: Visit times of a boundary orbit to a face
articles.statement: The times `i` in one period of the orbit of `a` at which the dart has face `f`.

articles.title: Boolean indicator of a decided proposition
articles.statement: The indicator `bI` of a decided proposition.

articles.title: Indicator of a Boolean
articles.statement: The indicator `1` or `0` of a Boolean.

articles.title: Agreement of the two edge counts of a cell complex
articles.statement: The two edge counts of a cell complex agree.

articles.title: Cardinality of an intersection as a sum of indicators
articles.statement: The size of `S ∩ T` as the sum over `T` of the indicator of `S`. See also `Finset.sum_boole`.

articles.title: Cardinality of a set difference as a sum of indicators
articles.statement: The size of `s \ t` as a sum of indicators.

articles.title: Distinct cells have distinct top edges
articles.statement: Distinct cells have distinct top edges.

articles.title: Cell degree of a lattice vertex
articles.statement: The number of cells of `K` having `v` as a corner.

articles.title: Edges of a cell complex
articles.statement: The edges of the cell complex `S`, encoded by doubled midpoints.

articles.title: Sides of a unit cell
articles.statement: The four sides of a unit cell, as unordered pairs of corners.

articles.title: Vertices of a cell complex
articles.statement: The vertices of the cell complex `S`: all corners of its cells.

articles.title: Agreement of the two vertex sets of a cell complex
articles.statement: The two vertex sets of a cell complex agree.

articles.title: Vertices of a cell complex after adding a cell
articles.statement: The vertices of `insert c S`.

articles.title: Corners of a unit cell
articles.statement: The four corners of a unit cell.

articles.title: Unit cell of the plane
articles.statement: A unit cell `[a, a + 1] × [b, b + 1]` of the plane, labelled by its lower left corner.

articles.title: Corner count at the bottom-left corner of a new cell
articles.statement: The corner count at the bottom-left corner of a cell `(x, y) ∉ S`.

articles.title: Corner count at the bottom-right corner of a new cell
articles.statement: The corner count at the bottom-right corner of a cell `(x, y) ∉ S`.

articles.title: Corner count as a count of the four surrounding cells
articles.statement: The corner count at `v` counts the cells of `S` among the four cells around `v`.

articles.title: Corner count after adding a cell
articles.statement: Adding a new cell `c` raises the corner count by one exactly at the corners of `c`.

articles.title: At most four cells meet at a lattice point
articles.statement: At most four cells meet at a lattice point.

articles.title: A lattice point has an incident cell iff it is a vertex
articles.statement: A lattice point has an incident cell iff it is a vertex of `S`.

articles.title: Corner count at the top-left corner of a new cell
articles.statement: The corner count at the top-left corner of a cell `(x, y) ∉ S`.

articles.title: Corner count at the top-right corner of a new cell
articles.statement: The corner count at the top-right corner of a cell `(x, y) ∉ S`.

articles.title: Corner count of a lattice point
articles.statement: The number of cells of `S` having the lattice point `v` as a corner.

articles.title: Corner defect of two diagonally touching cells
articles.statement: Two diagonally touching cells have corner defect `6`.

articles.title: Corner defect as a sum of vertex weights
articles.statement: The corner defect as a sum of vertex weights.

articles.title: Cell Gauss–Bonnet formula
articles.statement:
Cell Gauss–Bonnet formula: for every finite set of unit cells, convex corners minus reflex
 corners equals four times the Euler characteristic plus twice the number of pinch points.

articles.title: Change of the corner defect when a cell is added
articles.statement: Change of the corner defect when a new cell is added.

articles.title: Change of the corner defect in terms of eight neighbours
articles.statement:
The change of the corner defect when the cell `(x, y)` is added, in terms of its eight
 neighbours.

articles.title: A single cell has corner defect 4
articles.statement: A single cell has corner defect `4`.

articles.title: Corner defect of a set of unit cells
articles.statement:
The corner defect of `S`: the number of vertices with exactly one incident cell of `S` (convex
 corners) minus the number with exactly three (reflex corners).

articles.title: Corner weight agrees with its integer version
articles.statement: `cornerWeight` agrees with its integer version `icw`.

articles.title: Change of a vertex weight when one more cell is incident
articles.statement: The change of a vertex weight when one more cell becomes incident.

articles.title: Corner weight of a vertex
articles.statement:
The weight of a vertex with `k` incident cells in the corner defect: `1` if `k = 1`, `-1` if `k
 = 3`, and `0` otherwise.

articles.title: A unit cell has four distinct corners
articles.statement: A cell has four distinct corners.

articles.title: Four corners of a unit cell
articles.statement: The four corners of the unit cell with lower-left corner `c`.

articles.title: Angle defect at a lattice vertex
articles.statement: The angle defect at `v`, in quarter turns: `4 - 2 · edgeDeg K v + cellDeg K v`.

articles.title: Number of new edges when a cell is added
articles.statement: The number of new edges when a cell is added, given its four side neighbours.

articles.title: Number of new vertices when a cell is added
articles.statement: The number of new vertices when a cell is added, given its eight neighbours.

articles.title: Midpoint encoding of a lattice edge
articles.statement:
The lattice edge `{a, b}` encoded by the sum `a + b`, twice its midpoint; injective on unit
 edges.

articles.title: Edge degree of a lattice vertex
articles.statement: The number of edges of the region `K` incident to `v`.

articles.title: Four edges of a unit cell
articles.statement: The four edges of cell `c`, each encoded by twice its midpoint.

articles.title: Cell regions built by attaching cells along boundary arcs
articles.statement:
Regions built from a single cell by repeatedly attaching a new cell along a boundary arc: the
new cell adds one more edge than vertex, so the Euler characteristic is unchanged.

articles.title: Euler characteristic of two diagonally touching cells
articles.statement: Two diagonally touching cells have Euler characteristic `1`.

articles.title: Agreement of the two Euler characteristics of a cell complex
articles.statement: The Euler characteristic `eulerChar` agrees with `StatMech.CellEulerChar.regChi`.

articles.title: Change of the Euler characteristic when a cell is added
articles.statement:
Change of the Euler characteristic when a new cell is added: new vertices minus new edges plus
 one.

articles.title: Euler characteristic bound via the open-top skeleton
articles.statement:
If the open-top skeleton of `S` is connected, then `eulerChar S ≤ 1`. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.CellEulerFaithful.eulerChar_le_one_of_skeleton_connected`, which assumes
 connectivity of the full skeleton.

articles.title: A single cell has Euler characteristic 1
articles.statement: A single cell has Euler characteristic `1`.

articles.title: Euler characteristic of a cell complex
articles.statement: The Euler characteristic `V - E + F` of the closed cell complex formed by the cells of `S`.

articles.title: Failure of the cell Gauss–Bonnet formula without a pinch term
Integer-valued corner weight
articles.statement: The vertex weight `cornerWeight` extended to integers.

articles.title: Integer jump of the corner weight
articles.statement: The change of the vertex weight from `m` to `m + 1` incident cells.

articles.title: Edge codes of a unit cell are its doubled edge midpoints
articles.statement: The codes of the edges of a cell are `StatMech.Onsager.CellEuler.edgesOf`.

articles.title: Lattice edge to the lower neighbour
articles.statement: The lattice edge from `v` to its lower neighbour.

articles.title: Lattice edge to the left neighbour
articles.statement: The lattice edge from `v` to its left neighbour.

articles.title: Lattice edge to the right neighbour
articles.statement: The lattice edge from `v` to its right neighbour.

articles.title: Lattice edge to the upper neighbour
articles.statement: The lattice edge from `v` to its upper neighbour.

articles.title: Indicator of zero
articles.statement: The indicator of `m = 0`.

articles.title: Local change of the corner defect
articles.statement:
The change of the corner defect when a cell is added, given which of its eight neighbours are
 present (`e, w, n, s, ne, nw, se, sw`).

articles.title: Local cell Gauss–Bonnet identity
articles.statement:
Local cell Gauss–Bonnet identity: when a cell is added, the change of the corner defect is four
 times the change of the Euler characteristic plus twice the change of the number of pinch
 points.

articles.title: Failure of the local identity without a pinch term
articles.statement:
The change of the corner defect is not always four times the change of the Euler
 characteristic.

articles.title: Membership of a cell's bottom edge in the cell complex
articles.statement:
The horizontal edge with doubled midpoint `(2x + 1, 2y)` belongs to `S` iff one of the two cells
 it bounds does.

articles.title: Membership of a cell's left edge in the cell complex
articles.statement:
The vertical edge with doubled midpoint `(2x, 2y + 1)` belongs to `S` iff one of the two cells
 it bounds does.

articles.title: Membership of a cell's right edge in the cell complex
articles.statement:
The vertical edge with doubled midpoint `(2x + 2, 2y + 1)` belongs to `S` iff one of the two
 cells it bounds does.

articles.title: Membership of a cell's top edge in the cell complex
articles.statement:
The horizontal edge with doubled midpoint `(2x + 1, 2y + 2)` belongs to `S` iff one of the two
 cells it bounds does.

articles.title: Characterization of the corners of a unit cell
articles.statement: `v` is a corner of `c` iff `c` is one of the four cells around `v`.

articles.title: Number of new sides added by a cell
articles.statement: The number of sides of `c` that are not already edges of the region `K`.

articles.title: Number of new corners added by a cell
articles.statement: The number of corners of `c` that are not already vertices of the region `K`.

articles.title: Non-vertices are the points with no incident cell
articles.statement: A lattice point is not a vertex of `S` iff no cell of `S` is incident to it.

articles.title: Edges of the open-top skeleton
articles.statement: The edges of `openTopSkeleton S` are the edges of `S` other than top edges.

articles.title: Open-top skeleton of a cell complex
articles.statement:
The 1-skeleton of the cell complex `S` with the top edge of every cell removed, as a simple
 graph on its vertices.

articles.title: A pinch point is a vertex
articles.statement: A pinch point is a vertex of `S`.

articles.title: Pinch point of a set of unit cells
articles.statement:
The lattice point `v` is a pinch point of `S`: of the four cells around `v`, exactly two
 diagonally opposite ones belong to `S`.

articles.title: Pinch count changes only at the corners of a new cell
articles.statement: Adding a cell changes the pinch count only at the corners of that cell.

articles.title: Number of pinch points
articles.statement: The number of pinch points of `S`.

articles.title: Local change of the number of pinch points
articles.statement:
The change of the number of pinch points at the four corners of a new cell, given its eight
 neighbours.

articles.title: Change of the pinch indicator at the bottom-left corner of a new cell
articles.statement: Change of the pinch indicator at the bottom-left corner of a new cell.

articles.title: Change of the pinch indicator at the bottom-right corner of a new cell
articles.statement: Change of the pinch indicator at the bottom-right corner of a new cell.

articles.title: Change of the pinch indicator at the top-left corner of a new cell
articles.statement: Change of the pinch indicator at the top-left corner of a new cell.

articles.title: Change of the pinch indicator at the top-right corner of a new cell
articles.statement: Change of the pinch indicator at the top-right corner of a new cell.

articles.title: Change of the pinch count in terms of eight neighbours
articles.statement: The change of the pinch count when a cell is added, in terms of its eight neighbours.

articles.title: Pinch point indicator
articles.statement: The indicator of `v` being a pinch point of `S`.

articles.title: Regular Euler characteristic bound via the open-top skeleton
articles.statement: If the open-top skeleton of `S` is connected, then `regChi S ≤ 1`.

articles.title: Euler characteristic of a union of unit cells
articles.statement:
The Euler characteristic `V - E + F` of the union of the cells in `K`, with one face
per
cell.

articles.title: Edges of a union of unit cells
articles.statement: The edges of the union of the cells in `K`.

articles.title: Edge count bound for a connected open-top skeleton
articles.statement: If the open-top skeleton is connected, it has at least as many edges as vertices minus one.

articles.title: Vertices of a union of unit cells
articles.statement: The vertices of the union of the cells in `K`.

articles.title: Corrected right side of the local Gauss–Bonnet identity
articles.statement:
Four times the change of the Euler characteristic plus twice the change of the number of pinch
 points.

articles.title: Four times the local change of the Euler characteristic
articles.statement: Four times the change of the Euler characteristic when a cell is added.

articles.title: New edges of an added cell match the local count
articles.statement: The number of new edges when the cell `(x, y)` is added.

articles.title: New vertices of an added cell match the local count
articles.statement: The number of new vertices when the cell `(x, y)` is added.

articles.title: Double counting of cell–corner incidences
articles.statement: Double counting of cell–corner incidences: `∑ v, cornerCount S v = 4 * S.card`.

articles.title: Four cells around a lattice vertex
articles.statement: The four cells having `v` as a corner.

articles.title: Top edge of a unit cell
articles.statement: The top edge of the cell `c`.

articles.title: Top edges of a set of cells
articles.statement: The top edges of the cells of `S`.

articles.title: Lattice point as a vertex of the cell complex
articles.statement: A lattice point of `ℤ²`, used as a vertex of the cell complex.

articles.title: Number of convex corners of a lattice region
articles.statement: The number of vertices of the region with defect `1` (convex corners).

articles.title: Number of pinch points of a lattice region
articles.statement:
The number of vertices of the region with defect `-2` (pinch points, where two cells meet only
at a corner).

articles.title: Number of reflex corners of a lattice region
articles.statement: The number of vertices of the region with defect `-1` (reflex corners).

articles.title: Boundary edge of a set
articles.statement: The edge `e` has exactly one endpoint in `S`.

articles.title: Bounded regions are the components other than the outer one
articles.statement:
The finite components of the region graph are exactly the components other than the outer
region.

articles.title: Set of sites is the inside of a closed lattice walk
articles.statement:
Some closed lattice walk has odd ray count exactly at the sites of `K`, so `K` is the inside
of that walk.

articles.title: Four unit faces at a lattice site
articles.statement: The four unit faces having the site `c` as a corner.

articles.title: Number of boundary crossings of a walk
articles.statement: The number of edges of the walk `w` with exactly one endpoint in `S`.

articles.title: Inside and outside of a closed walk are connected
articles.statement:
The inside and the outside of `Vc` are nonempty and each is connected in the lattice with the
boundary edges of the inside removed. This is `StatMech.Lattice.jcs_JordanRegion
(jec_leftRegion Vc)`.

articles.title: Every edge of a finite even-degree graph lies on a cycle
articles.statement:
In a finite graph in which every vertex has even degree, every edge lies on a cycle. See also
Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.adj_and_reachable_delete_edges_iff_exists_cycle`, which this combines
with `StatMech.Lattice.reachable_deleteEdges_of_even`.

articles.title: Box exterior embeds in the region graph
articles.statement: Outside a box containing the image of `P`, the lattice embeds in the region graph.

articles.title: Face-boundary graph of a set
articles.statement:
The face-boundary graph of `S`: two adjacent faces are joined when the primal edge between
them has exactly one endpoint in `S`. Its edges are the dual edges crossing the boundary of
`S`.

articles.title: Lattice off a closed walk
articles.statement: The subgraph of the square lattice induced on the sites not visited by `Vc`.

articles.title: Jordan region property off a closed walk
articles.statement:
Both sides of `Vc` contain sites off `Vc`, and any two sites off `Vc` on the same side are
joined by a lattice path avoiding `Vc`.

articles.title: Flood fill avoiding a set of sites
articles.statement:
The flood fill of `seed` avoiding `B`: the sites reachable from `seed` in the lattice with
`B` removed.

articles.title: Lattice walk avoiding a set, lifted to the reduced lattice
articles.statement: A lattice walk avoiding `B`, viewed as a walk in `ffc_offSupportLattice B`.

articles.title: Square lattice with a set of vertices removed
articles.statement: The square lattice with every vertex of `B` removed (edges with an endpoint in `B` deleted).

articles.title: Geometric count of bounded regions
articles.statement: The number of finite connected components of the region graph of `P`.

articles.title: Image of a planar lattice subgraph in the square lattice
articles.statement: The image of a `PlanarZ2Subgraph` as a subgraph of the square lattice.

articles.title: Disconnected sites are joined in the lattice minus a bridged graph
articles.statement:
If `x` and `y` are not connected in `K`, they are connected in the lattice minus the image of
`K ⊔ edge x y`.

articles.title: Corners of the unit square in cyclic order
articles.statement: The four corners `(0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1)` of the unit square, in cyclic order.

articles.title: Adjacency relation of the 4-cycle
articles.statement: Adjacency of the 4-cycle `0 – 1 – 2 – 3 – 0`, as a Boolean relation.

articles.title: The 4-cycle graph
articles.statement: The 4-cycle on `Fin 4`.

articles.title: Square lattice minus the edges of a graph
articles.statement: The square lattice with the edges of `H` deleted.

articles.title: Unit square as a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement: The unit square: the 4-cycle embedded on the corners of `[0, 1]²`.

articles.title: Quarter-turn isomorphism onto the region graph
articles.statement:
The quarter-turn rotation is an isomorphism from the lattice minus the edges of `H` onto the
region graph of `H`.

articles.title: Vertex 0 of the 4-cycle
articles.statement: The vertex `0` of the 4-cycle.

articles.title: Vertex 1 of the 4-cycle
articles.statement: The vertex `1` of the 4-cycle.

articles.title: Bounded regions indexed by the cycle rank
articles.statement:
The bijection between bounded regions of `P` and `Fin (nullity P.G)` given by the discrete
Jordan–Euler theorem.

articles.title: Bounded regions of a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement: The bounded (finite) connected components of the face-region graph of `P`.

articles.title: Two diagonally touching sites
articles.statement: The two-site set `{(0, 0), (1, 1)}`, which touches diagonally.

articles.title: Adjacency relation of the 8-cycle
articles.statement: Adjacency of the 8-cycle on `Fin 8`, as a Boolean relation.

articles.title: The 8-cycle graph
articles.statement: The 8-cycle on `Fin 8`.

articles.title: Lattice points around the L-shaped tromino
articles.statement: The eight lattice points around the L-shaped tromino, in cyclic order.

articles.title: 8-cycle around the L-tromino as a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement: The 8-cycle around the L-shaped tromino as a `PlanarZ2Subgraph`.

articles.title: Jordan curve theorem
articles.statement:
**Jordan curve theorem** for lattice cycles: a connected `PlanarZ2Subgraph` with as many
edges as vertices has exactly one bounded region. Reference: C. Jordan, *Cours d'analyse*
(1887); for the discrete form, C. Thomassen, *The Jordan–Schönflies theorem and the
classification of surfaces* (1992).

articles.title: Cycle rank one gives a unique bounded region
articles.statement: A `PlanarZ2Subgraph` of cycle rank one has exactly one bounded region.

articles.title: Jordan curve theorem for cycles: face count two
articles.statement:
A cycle, as a graph on its own vertices, has face count two: the combinatorial form of the
**Jordan curve theorem** for cycles (C. Jordan, *Cours d'analyse*, 1887).

articles.title: Jordan region of the cut lattice
articles.statement:
`S` and its complement are nonempty, and any two sites on the same side of `S` are connected
in the lattice with the boundary edges of `S` removed.

articles.title: Separating side between inside and outside sites
articles.statement:
Some set `S` contains `inside`, misses `outside`, and every lattice edge between sites of `D`
that leaves `S` has an endpoint in `B`.

articles.title: Adjacency relation of the lower 4-cycle
articles.statement: Adjacency of the lower 4-cycle, as a Boolean relation.

articles.title: Lower 4-cycle left after deleting the upper one
articles.statement: The lower 4-cycle, which remains after deleting the upper one.

articles.title: Upper 4-cycle based at the shared vertex
articles.statement: The 4-cycle of the upper square, based at the shared vertex.

articles.title: Vertices of two unit squares sharing a corner
articles.statement: The vertices of two unit squares `[0, 1]²` and `[1, 2]²` sharing the corner `(1, 1)`.

articles.title: Two 4-cycles sharing a vertex
articles.statement: Two 4-cycles sharing the vertex `2`, on `Fin 7`.

articles.title: Two corner-sharing unit squares as a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement: Two unit squares sharing a corner as a `PlanarZ2Subgraph`.

articles.title: Adjacency relation of two corner-sharing squares
articles.statement: Adjacency of the two squares sharing a corner, as a Boolean relation.

articles.title: Even-degree subgraphs have as many regions as their face count
articles.statement:
Every subgraph `K` of `P` whose image has all degrees even has exactly `faceCount K`
face-region components.

articles.title: Peeling a cycle from an even-degree subgraph
articles.statement:
Every nonempty subgraph `K` of `P` whose image has all degrees even contains a subgraph of
the same kind with fewer edges, face count one less, and one fewer face-region component.

articles.title: Even-peelable graph
articles.statement:
`K` reduces to the empty graph by repeatedly deleting a cycle through a base vertex `v` such
that, after the deletion, the other vertices of the cycle are isolated.

articles.title: Even-degree condition on a subgraph
articles.statement: Every vertex of `K` has even degree.

articles.title: Half-plane below a row
articles.statement: The half-plane of sites in rows below `y`.

articles.title: Open vertical crossings separate the sides of a rectangle
articles.statement:
For every configuration, every overlap rectangle, and every `α < β`, `c ≤ d`, the arc-side
property `StatMech.Universality.CrossingArcSides` holds: an open vertical crossing of the
overlap separates the left side of `[α, β] × [c, d]` from its right side.

articles.title: Horizontal lattice path rightward
articles.statement: The horizontal lattice path from `(t, row)` right to `(t + k, row)`.

articles.title: Inside of a closed walk by the even-odd rule
articles.statement:
The inside of a closed walk `Vc` by the even–odd rule: sites whose ray count with respect to
`Vc` is odd.

articles.title: Quadrant below and left of a site
articles.statement: The quadrant of sites `p` with `p 0 ≤ z 0 - 1` and `p 1 ≤ z 1 - 1`.

articles.title: Ray-crossing count of a walk
articles.statement: The number of ray edges of `z` traversed by the walk `w`.

articles.title: Ray edges left of a site
articles.statement:
The vertical lattice edges in a column left of `z` joining rows `z 1 - 1` and `z 1`: the
edges crossed by a horizontal ray going left from the face corner of `z`.

articles.title: Return path around a rectangle
articles.statement:
A lattice path from `(b0, d)` back to `(a0, c)` running outside the rectangle `[α, β] × [c,
d]`: up, left to column `α - 1`, down to row `c - 1`, right, and up.

articles.title: Vertical lattice path upward
articles.statement: The vertical lattice path from `(col, r)` up to `(col, r + k)`.

articles.title: Wall-crossing count of a walk
articles.statement: The number of wall edges of `z` traversed by the walk `w`.

articles.title: Wall edges below a site
articles.statement:
The horizontal lattice edges in a row below `z` joining columns `z 0 - 1` and `z 0`: the
edges crossed by a vertical ray going down from the face corner of `z`.

articles.title: Twelve boundary edges of a 3 by 3 rectangle
articles.statement: The twelve lattice edges of the boundary of the rectangle `[-1, 2] × [-2, 1]`.

articles.title: Boundary of a 3 by 3 rectangle as a graph
articles.statement: The boundary of the rectangle `[-1, 2] × [-2, 1]` as a graph.

articles.title: Cut set of a face coloring
articles.statement:
The primal edges `sharedPrimalEdge a b` between adjacent faces `a`, `b` on which `T` takes
different values.

articles.title: Bounded faces of a finite lattice graph are counted by its cycle rank
articles.statement:
For a
`PlanarZ2Subgraph` `P`, the finite components of the face-region graph `whb_faceRegion` of its
image (faces of `ℤ²`, two adjacent faces joined unless the primal edge between them lies in `P`)
are equinumerous with `Fin (nullity P.G)`, so the number of bounded faces is `|E| - |V| + c`.
This is a count: it does not identify each bounded face with the interior of a particular cycle
of `P`. References: H. Whitney, *Planar graphs* (1933); C. Thomassen, *The Jordan–Schönflies
theorem and the classification of surfaces* (1992).

articles.title: Lattice graph spanned by an edge set
articles.statement: The graph on `ℤ²` whose edges are the lattice edges in `E`.

articles.title: Pushforward of a subgraph into the square lattice
articles.statement: The image in `ℤ²` of a subgraph `K` of a `PlanarZ2Subgraph` `P`.

articles.title: Bounded region count as cycle rank
articles.statement: The number of bounded regions of a finite graph, defined as its cycle rank `nullity G`.

articles.title: Whitney duality for even-degree planar lattice subgraphs
articles.statement: Every `PlanarZ2Subgraph` whose image has all degrees even satisfies `jfc_WhbSync`.

articles.title: Pushed-forward subgraphs are locally finite
articles.statement: The image of a subgraph of a `PlanarZ2Subgraph` is locally finite.

articles.title: Interior region of the unit square
articles.statement: The component of the face `(0, 0)` in the face-region graph of the unit square.

articles.title: Outer face region of a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement:
The outer region: the component of the face-region graph of `P` containing a face far from
`P`.

articles.title: Whitney cut-cycle duality for a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement:
Whitney's cut–cycle duality for `P`: for every subgraph `K` of `P` and edge `xy` of `P` not
in `K`, with `f0g0` the dual edge across it, `x` and `y` are connected in `K` iff `f0` and
`g0` are disconnected in the face-region graph of `K` with `f0g0` deleted.

articles.title: Exterior of a box maps into the face-region graph
articles.statement:
For `H` and `f0g0` inside `[-R, R]²`, the lattice on the exterior of `[-(R + 1), R + 1]²`
maps into the face-region graph of `H` with `f0g0` deleted.

articles.title: Cactus graph, defined by peeling leaves and cycles
articles.statement:
`K` reduces to the empty graph by repeatedly deleting a leaf edge or, when `K` is a union of
cycles, one of its cycles.

articles.title: 4-cycle core of the pendant example
articles.statement: The 4-cycle on `0, 1, 2, 3` inside `Fin 5`.

articles.title: Unit square corners with a pendant site
articles.statement: The corners of the unit square together with the site `(-1, 0)`.

articles.title: 4-cycle with a pendant edge
articles.statement: The 4-cycle with a pendant edge, on `Fin 5`.

articles.title: Unit square with a pendant edge as a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement: The unit square with a pendant edge as a `PlanarZ2Subgraph`.

articles.title: Adjacency relation of a 4-cycle with a pendant edge
articles.statement:
Adjacency of the 4-cycle on `0, 1, 2, 3` with the pendant edge `{0, 4}`, as a Boolean
relation.

articles.title: Number of face regions of a subgraph's image
articles.statement: The number of connected components of the face-region graph of the image of `K`.

articles.title: Corners of two distant unit squares
articles.statement: The corners of the unit squares at `(0, 0)` and `(10, 0)`.

articles.title: Two disjoint 4-cycles
articles.statement: Two disjoint 4-cycles on `Fin 8`.

articles.title: Two disjoint unit squares as a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement: Two disjoint unit squares as a `PlanarZ2Subgraph`.

articles.title: Adjacency relation of two disjoint 4-cycles
articles.statement: Adjacency of two disjoint 4-cycles on `Fin 8`, as a Boolean relation.

articles.title: The 3 by 3 grid graph
articles.statement: The `3 × 3` grid graph on `Fin 9`.

articles.title: Nine sites of a 3 by 3 grid
articles.statement: The nine sites of `[0, 2]²`, indexed row by row.

articles.title: Adjacency relation of the 3 by 3 grid
articles.statement: Adjacency of the `3 × 3` grid on `Fin 9`, as a Boolean relation.

articles.title: Grid vertex $(0, 0)$
articles.statement: The vertex `(0, 0)` of the grid.

articles.title: Grid vertex $(1, 0)$
articles.statement: The vertex `(1, 0)` of the grid.

articles.title: 3 by 3 grid as a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement: The `3 × 3` grid as a `PlanarZ2Subgraph`.

articles.title: Keep-reconnect residue for finite graphs
articles.statement:
For every graph `H` of `ℤ²` with finitely many edges and every lattice edge `pq` outside `H`
with dual edge `f0g0`: if `p` and `q` are disconnected in `H`, then `f0` and `g0` are
connected in the face-region graph of `H` with `f0g0` deleted.

articles.title: Horizontal axis with one edge removed
articles.statement: The horizontal axis of `ℤ²` with the edge from `(0, 0)` to `(1, 0)` removed.

articles.title: Adjacency relation of the cut horizontal axis
articles.statement: Both sites lie on the horizontal axis and the pair is not `{(0, 0), (1, 0)}`.

articles.title: Adding an edge between two components merges them
articles.statement:
Adding an edge between two components merges them. This assumes only finitely many
components; see also `StatMech.Lattice.card_components_sup_edge_of_not_reachable` for finite
vertex types.

articles.title: Veblen's theorem step for unions of cycles
articles.statement:
One step of **Veblen's theorem** (O. Veblen, 1912) for graphs whose vertices all have degree
zero or two: a nonempty such graph has a subgraph of the same kind with fewer edges and face count
one less (obtained by deleting a cycle).

articles.title: Region step property for even-degree subgraphs
articles.statement:
Whenever `K' ≤ K` are even-degree subgraphs of `P` with fewer edges and face count one less,
the face-region graph of `K` has one more component than that of `K'`.

articles.title: Veblen step property for even-degree subgraphs
articles.statement:
Every nonempty subgraph `K` of `P` with even-degree image contains an even-degree subgraph
with fewer edges and face count one less.

articles.title: Square lattice with the boundary edges of a set removed
articles.statement: The square lattice with every edge having exactly one endpoint in `S` removed.

articles.title: Component off a closed walk containing a seed
articles.statement: The sites reachable from `seed` in the lattice with the vertices of `Vc` removed.

articles.title: Square lattice with a closed walk's vertices removed
articles.statement:
The square lattice with the vertices of the closed walk `Vc` removed. It is the same graph as
`StatMech.Lattice.ffc_offSupportLattice {z | z ∈ Vc.support}`.

articles.title: Radius of a box containing a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement: A radius `R` such that the image of `P` lies in `box 2 R`.

articles.title: Outer region of the rotated region graph
articles.statement: The outer region: the component of the region graph containing the far site `beacon 2 R`.

articles.title: Planar lattice subgraph of the square lattice
articles.statement: A finite graph together with an injective map into `ℤ²` that sends edges to lattice edges.

articles.title: Rotated region graph of a lattice subgraph
articles.statement:
The square lattice with the edge `crossEdge e` removed for every edge `e` of `G`. Since
`crossEdge` is a global rotation, this is not the faithful dual complement; see
`StatMech.Lattice.whb_faceRegion` for the version using `sharedPrimalEdge`.

articles.title: Boundary darts of a component off a closed walk
articles.statement: The set of boundary darts of a connected component of the sites off the support of `Vc`.

articles.title: Facial orbit of a boundary dart
articles.statement:
The orbit of a boundary dart of `C`, as a connected component of the successor graph on
boundary darts.

articles.title: Facial orbits cover the components of the complement
articles.statement:
The boundary dart sets of the components of the complement of `Vc` are exactly the members of
`𝓕`.

articles.title: Primal edge shared by adjacent faces
articles.statement:
The primal edge of `ℤ²` separating the adjacent unit faces with lower left corners `f` and
`g`.

articles.title: Unit squares of the grid $(-n, n)^2$
articles.statement: The unit squares of the grid `[-n, n]²`, labelled by their lower left corners.

articles.title: Edges of the grid $(-n, n)^2$
articles.statement: The edges of the grid `[-n, n]²`.

articles.title: Euler's formula for the grid graph $(-n, n)^2$
articles.statement:
Euler's formula `V - E + F = 2` for the planar grid graph `[-n, n]²`, with faces counted
geometrically (unit squares plus the unbounded face).

articles.title: Number of faces of the grid $(-n, n)^2$
articles.statement: The number of faces of the grid `[-n, n]²`: its unit squares and the unbounded face.

articles.title: Square lattice induced on the box $(-n, n)^2$
articles.statement: The subgraph of the square lattice induced on the box `[-n, n]²`.

articles.title: Vertices of the grid $(-n, n)^2$
articles.statement: The vertices of the grid `[-n, n]²`.

articles.title: Edgeless graph has one component per vertex
articles.statement: The edgeless graph has one component per vertex.

articles.title: Adding a new edge increases the edge count by one
articles.statement:
Adding a new edge increases the number of edges by one. This is the `Set.ncard` form of
Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.card_edgeFinset_sup_edge`.

articles.title: Removing one element lowers cardinality by one
articles.statement:
Removing one element from a finite type lowers its cardinality by one. See also Mathlib's
`Fintype.card_subtype_compl`.

articles.title: Connected graph with $|V| - 1$ edges is acyclic, and conversely
articles.statement:
A connected finite graph has exactly `|V| - 1` edges iff it is acyclic. See also Mathlib's
`SimpleGraph.isTree_iff_connected_and_card` and `SimpleGraph.IsTree.card_edgeFinset`.

articles.title: Connected finite graph has at least $|V| - 1$ edges
articles.statement:
A connected finite graph has at least `|V| - 1` edges. This is the `Fintype` form of Mathlib's
`SimpleGraph.Connected.card_vert_le_card_edgeSet_add_one`.

articles.title: Cyclomatic number $|E| + 1 - |V|$ of a finite graph
articles.statement:
The cyclomatic number `|E| + 1 - |V|` of a finite graph. For a connected graph it is the
dimension of the cycle space. See `StatMech.Lattice.nullity` for the version for arbitrary
finite graphs.

articles.title: Graph stays connected with a given bridge after deleting edges
articles.statement: After deleting the edges `B'`, the graph `A` is connected and `{a, b}` is one of its bridges.

articles.title: Euler's formula solved for the number of components
articles.statement: Euler's formula solved for the number of components: `c = |V| - |E| + F - 1`.

articles.title: Euler's formula
articles.statement:
**Euler's formula** for a finite graph with `c` connected components: `|V| - |E| + F = 1 + c`,
where `F = faceCount G`.

Here `F` is defined as the cycle rank plus one, so the statement is the combinatorial Euler
relation; it agrees with `StatMech.Lattice.euler_relation_sub` up to the order of the summands. That
`F` counts the faces of a plane embedding is a separate statement; for finite subgraphs of the
square lattice the bounded faces are counted in `StatMech.Lattice.jed_faithfulDiscreteJordan`.
Reference: L. Euler, *Elementa doctrinae solidorum* (1758).

articles.title: Combinatorial Euler relation for finite graphs
articles.statement:
The combinatorial Euler relation `|V| + F = |E| + c + 1` for a finite graph, where `F =
faceCount G` is defined from the cycle rank.

articles.title: Face count of a finite graph from its cycle rank
articles.statement:
The face count `nullity G + 1`. For a finite subgraph of `ℤ²` it is the number of faces,
including the unbounded one (`StatMech.Lattice.jed_faithfulDiscreteJordan` counts the bounded
ones); as a definition it is purely combinatorial.

articles.title: Horizontal edges of the grid $(-n, n)^2$
articles.statement: The horizontal edges of the grid `[-n, n]²`.

articles.title: Cycle rank of a finite graph
articles.statement:
The cycle rank (nullity, first Betti number) `|E| + c - |V|` of a finite graph, where `c` is the
number of connected components.

articles.title: Successive deletion of non-bridge edges
articles.statement:
Deleting the edges of `L` from the last to the first, each edge is a non-bridge at the moment
it is deleted.

articles.title: Deleting a list of edges from a graph
articles.statement: `A` with the edges of the list `L` deleted.

articles.title: Three-step detour avoiding an edge
articles.statement:
The edge `e = {a, b}` has a three-step detour `a, a', b', b` in `A` none of whose edges is
`e` or lies in `L`.

articles.title: Non-bridge edge of a graph
articles.statement: `e` is an edge of `A` whose endpoints remain connected after `e` is deleted.

articles.title: Vertical edges of the grid $(-n, n)^2$
articles.statement: The vertical edges of the grid `[-n, n]²`.

articles.title: Adjacency in the complete graph
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$ and all vertices $x$ and $y$
of the complete graph $K_n$, whose vertices are the natural numbers less than $n$, $x$ and $y$ are
adjacent if and only if $x \ne y$.

articles.title: Complete graph as a finite graph
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $K_n$ is the finite graph whose
vertices are the natural numbers less than $n$, in which any two distinct vertices are adjacent.

articles.title: Finite simple graph
articles.statement:
A finite graph consists of a finite vertex set $V$ together with a
simple graph on $V$, that is, a symmetric and irreflexive adjacency relation on $V$.

Stable source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robertson%E2%80%93Seymour_theorem.

articles.title: Graph minor relation
articles.statement:
For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, $H$ is a minor of $G$ when there is a
finite sequence $H = G_0, G_1, \dots, G_k = G$ of finite graphs, with $k \ge 0$, such that for
each $i < k$, $G_i$ arises from $G_{i+1}$ by one minor step: an isomorphism, the deletion of one
vertex, the deletion of one edge, or the contraction of one edge.

Stable source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robertson%E2%80%93Seymour_theorem.

articles.title: One-step graph minor
articles.statement:
For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, $H$ arises from $G$ by one minor step
when one of the following holds. Isomorphism: $H$ is isomorphic to $G$. Vertex deletion: for some
vertex $a$ of $G$ there is an injective map $f$ from the vertices of $H$ to the vertices of $G$
whose image consists of all vertices other than $a$, such that vertices $u, v$ of $H$ are adjacent
exactly when $f(u), f(v)$ are adjacent in $G$. Edge deletion: for some edge $xy$ of $G$ there is a
bijection $e$ from the vertices of $H$ to the vertices of $G$ such that, for all vertices $u, v$ of
$H$, the vertices $e(u), e(v)$ are adjacent in $G$ whenever $u, v$ are adjacent in $H$, and if
$e(u), e(v)$ are adjacent in $G$, then either $u, v$ are adjacent in $H$ or the pair $(e(u), e(v))$
is $(x, y)$ or $(y, x)$; moreover, $e^{-1}(x), e^{-1}(y)$ are not adjacent in $H$. Edge
contraction: for some edge $ab$ of $G$ there is a surjective map $f$ from the vertices of $G$ to
the vertices of $H$ with $f(a) = f(b)$ such that, for all vertices $x, y$ of $G$, $f(x) = f(y)$
implies $x = y$ or $(x, y)$ is $(a, b)$ or $(b, a)$, and vertices $u, v$ of $H$ are adjacent
exactly when $u \ne v$ and there are adjacent vertices $u', v'$ of $G$ with $f(u') = u$ and
$f(v') = v$.

Stable source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robertson%E2%80%93Seymour_theorem.

articles.title: An isomorphic copy is a minor
articles.statement:
For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, if $H$ is isomorphic to $G$,
then $H$ is a minor of $G$.

articles.title: A single minor step gives a minor
articles.statement:
For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, if $H$ arises from $G$ by
one minor step, then $H$ is a minor of $G$.

articles.title: Reflexivity of the graph minor relation
articles.statement: Every finite graph $G$ is a minor of itself.

articles.title: Robertson–Seymour theorem
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a family of finite simple graphs that is closed
under taking minors: whenever $G \in F$ and $H$ is a minor of $G$, also $H \in F$. Then any two
finite graphs that are minors of each other are isomorphic, and there is a finite set $O$ of
finite graphs such that a finite graph $G$ belongs to $F$ if and only if no graph in $O$ is a
minor of $G$.

Stable source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robertson%E2%80%93Seymour_theorem.

articles.title: Transitivity of the graph minor relation
articles.statement:
For finite graphs $H$, $K$ and $G$, if $H$ is a
minor of $K$ and $K$ is a minor of $G$, then $H$ is a minor of $G$.

articles.title: Exactly four left turns when simplicity rules out eight
articles.statement:
A closed walk with only straight steps and left turns has exactly four left turns, provided
 simplicity rules out eight or more.

articles.title: A closed walk without right turns turns at least once
articles.statement: A closed walk with only straight steps and left turns turns at least once.

articles.title: Number of left turns of a direction sequence
articles.statement:
The number of counterclockwise (left) quarter turns of the cyclic direction sequence `d`, i.e.
 of indices `i` with `d (i + 1) - d i = 1`.

articles.title: Without right turns, the number of left turns is divisible by four
articles.statement: If every turn is straight or left, the number of left turns is divisible by `4`.

articles.title: A closed walk without right turns has at least four left turns
articles.statement: A closed walk with only straight steps and left turns has at least four left turns.

articles.title: North step followed by west step at the top corner of a walk
articles.statement:
A closed walk with only straight steps and left turns has a north step immediately followed by a
 west step (at its lexicographically largest vertex).

articles.title: Previous and next vertices of a north-then-west corner
articles.statement:
At a north-then-west corner `M`, the previous vertex is just below and the next vertex just to
 the left.

articles.title: Distinct north-then-west corners sit at distinct vertices
articles.statement: In a simple walk, distinct north-then-west corners sit at distinct vertices.

articles.title: Reverse of a dart
articles.statement: The reverse of a dart: it starts at the head of `d` and points in the opposite direction.

articles.title: Integer turn exponent between two directions
articles.statement:
The integer turn exponent from `μ` to `ν`: `1` for a left turn, `-1` for a right turn, `0` for
going straight (and, by convention, for a U-turn).

articles.title: Turn between two directions as an element of $\mathbb{Z}/4$
articles.statement: The turn from direction `μ` to `ν` as an element of `ZMod 4`.

articles.title: Backward vertex recursion of a closed lattice walk
articles.statement: Vertex recursion of a closed walk read backwards from vertex `M`.

articles.title: Forward vertex recursion of a closed lattice walk
articles.statement:
Vertex recursion of a closed walk: the next vertex is the current one plus the current step
 (indices taken cyclically).

articles.title: Closed lattice walk starts at the origin
articles.statement: The walk starts at the origin.

articles.title: Vertices of a lattice walk from its step directions
articles.statement:
The `k`-th vertex of the lattice walk with step directions `d`: the sum of the steps `stepOf (d
 i)` for `i < k`, so that `pos d 0 = 0`.

articles.title: Coordinates of the four lattice steps
articles.statement: The four lattice steps, case by case.

articles.title: Unit lattice step in a given direction
articles.statement:
The unit step of `ℤ²` in direction `w`: `0 ↦ (1, 0)` (east), `1 ↦ (0, 1)` (north), `2 ↦ (-1, 0)`
 (west), `3 ↦ (0, -1)` (south).

articles.title: Turns of a cyclic direction sequence sum to zero
articles.statement: The turns of a cyclic direction sequence sum to zero in `Fin 4`.

articles.title: North-then-west corner at the highest vertices
articles.statement:
A closed walk without right turns has a north-then-west corner at the rightmost of its highest
 vertices.

articles.title: South-then-east corner at the lowest vertices
articles.statement: A closed walk without right turns has a south-then-east corner at one of its lowest vertices.

articles.title: Left turns are four times the north-to-west turns
articles.statement:
In a direction sequence without right turns, the number of left turns is four times the number
 of north-to-west turns.

articles.title: A unique top corner forces fewer than eight left turns
articles.statement:
If the north-then-west corner is unique, a direction sequence without right turns has fewer than
 eight left turns.

articles.title: Eight left turns give two north-then-west corners
articles.statement: Eight or more left turns, without right turns, give two distinct north-then-west corners.

articles.title: Recursion for the x-coordinate of a walk step
articles.statement:
The `x`-coordinate recursion of a closed walk. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.NoDoubleWind2.xco_succ`.

articles.title: A closed walk crosses each horizontal line an even number of times
articles.statement: A closed walk crosses each horizontal line `y = m + 1/2` an even number of times.

articles.title: Number of crossings of a horizontal line
articles.statement:
The number of vertical steps of the walk crossing the horizontal line `y = m + 1/2`, i.e.
 vertical steps between heights `m` and `m + 1`.

articles.title: Horizontal lattice direction
articles.statement: The direction `w` is horizontal (east or west).

articles.title: Vertical lattice direction
articles.statement: The direction `w` is vertical (north or south).

articles.title: No east step leaves a rightmost vertex
articles.statement: No east step leaves a vertex of maximal `x`-coordinate.

articles.title: No west step arrives at a rightmost vertex
articles.statement: No west step arrives at a vertex of maximal `x`-coordinate.

articles.title: No north step arrives at a lowest vertex
articles.statement: No north step arrives at a vertex of minimal `y`-coordinate.

articles.title: No south step leaves a lowest vertex
articles.statement: No south step leaves a vertex of minimal `y`-coordinate.

articles.title: Number of straight continuations in a given direction
articles.statement: The number of straight continuations of `d` in direction `c`.

articles.title: Recursion for the y-coordinate of a walk step
articles.statement:
The `y`-coordinate recursion of a closed walk. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.NoDoubleWind2.yco_succ`.

articles.title: Every direction is left by equally many left turns
articles.statement:
In a direction sequence without right turns, every direction is left by the same number of left
 turns.

articles.title: Number of left turns out of a given direction
articles.statement: The number of left turns of `d` from direction `c` to direction `c + 1`.

articles.title: Contiguous top row of a walk
articles.statement:
The vertices of the walk at its maximal height cover every lattice point between any two of
 them, i.e. the top row of the walk is a contiguous horizontal segment.

articles.title: A closed walk crosses a horizontal line equally often up and down
articles.statement: A closed walk crosses the line `y = m + 1/2` upwards as often as downwards.

articles.title: Recursion for the x-coordinate of a closed walk
articles.statement:
The `x`-coordinate recursion of a closed walk. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.WalkCrossing.fst_step`.

articles.title: Recursion for the y-coordinate of a closed walk
articles.statement:
The `y`-coordinate recursion of a closed walk. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.WalkCrossing.snd_step`.

articles.title: Four left turns, given that two corners force a self-intersection
articles.statement:
A simple closed walk without right turns has four left turns, assuming that two distinct
 north-then-west corners force a self-intersection.

articles.title: Crossing steps force a repeated vertex
articles.statement:
If a horizontal and a vertical step that share no index endpoint meet at a point, the walk
 visits some vertex twice.

articles.title: Existence of a north-then-west corner
articles.statement: A closed walk without right turns has a north-then-west corner.

articles.title: Moving horizontally inside a closed walk
articles.statement:
If cell `(a, b)` is inside and no vertical step separates it from `(a + 1, b)`, then `(a + 1,
 b)` is inside.

articles.title: Moving vertically inside a closed walk
articles.statement:
If cell `(a, b)` is inside and no horizontal step separates it from `(a, b + 1)`, then `(a, b +
 1)` is inside.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the lexicographically largest vertex
articles.statement: In a simple walk the lexicographically largest vertex is attained at a unique index.

articles.title: Coordinates of the vertices around a north-then-west corner
articles.statement: The vertices before and after a north-then-west corner.

articles.title: The north step at a corner blocks horizontal movement
articles.statement:
At a north-then-west corner, the north step separates the cell below-left of the corner from its
 right neighbour.

articles.title: The west step at a corner blocks vertical movement
articles.statement:
At a north-then-west corner, the west step separates the cell below-left of the corner from its
 top neighbour.

articles.title: A lattice point lies on a walk step
articles.statement: The lattice point `p` lies on the closed segment traversed by step `k`.

articles.title: Number of crossings of a horizontal ray
articles.statement:
The number of vertical steps crossing the line `y = m + 1/2` strictly to the right of `x =
 qx`.

articles.title: Ray parity is unchanged across a horizontal move
articles.statement:
The ray parity is the same for cells `(a, b)` and `(a + 1, b)` when no vertical step lies
 between them.

articles.title: Cells above a walk are outside
articles.statement: Cells at or above the top height of the walk are outside.

articles.title: Ray parity is unchanged across a vertical move
articles.statement:
The ray parity is the same for cells `(a, b)` and `(a, b + 1)` when no horizontal step lies
 between them.

articles.title: Ray-crossing parity of a lattice cell
articles.statement:
The parity of the number of crossings of the upward ray from the center of cell `(a, b)` with
 the walk; cells with parity `1` are inside the walk.

articles.title: Two north-then-west corners force a self-intersection
articles.statement: Any two distinct north-then-west corners of `d` force `pos d` to be non-injective.

articles.title: Upward crossing counts of horizontal neighbours sum to an even number
articles.statement:
When no vertical step separates the cells `(a, b)` and `(a + 1, b)`, their upward crossing
 counts add up to an even number.

articles.title: No upward crossings for cells above a walk
articles.statement: Cells at or above the top height of the walk have no upward crossings.

articles.title: Upward crossing count is unchanged across a vertical move
articles.statement:
The upward crossing count is the same for cells `(a, b)` and `(a, b + 1)` when no horizontal
 step lies between them.

articles.title: Upward ray crossings above a cell
articles.statement:
The number of horizontal steps of the walk on the column `[a, a + 1]` strictly above the cell
 `(a, b)`: the crossings of the upward vertical ray from the center of that cell.

articles.title: Index of a horizontal step right of a walk vertex
articles.statement:
In a simple walk, a horizontal step on the segment to the right of the vertex `pos d m` is step
 `m` or step `m - 1`.

articles.title: Index of a horizontal step left of a walk vertex
articles.statement:
In a simple walk, a horizontal step on the segment to the left of the vertex `pos d m` is step
 `m` or step `m - 1`.

articles.title: Steps around a left turn share their left cell
articles.statement: At a left turn, the steps before and after the turn have the same left cell.

articles.title: Left cells keep their ray parity on a straight step
articles.statement: Going straight, consecutive left cells have the same ray parity.

articles.title: Unit cell to the left of a lattice step
articles.statement:
The unit cell to the left of the step in direction `w` starting at `p` (cells are named by their
 lower-left corners).

articles.title: Left parity is constant along a walk without right turns
articles.statement: For a simple closed walk without right turns, the left parity is the same for every step.

articles.title: Consecutive steps have the same left parity
articles.statement: For a simple closed walk without right turns, consecutive steps have the same left parity.

articles.title: Ray parity of the cell left of a step
articles.statement: The ray parity of the cell to the left of step `k`.

articles.title: Horizontal steps on a unit segment
articles.statement: The horizontal steps of the walk on the segment `[a, a + 1] × {b}`.

articles.title: No horizontal step starts at a non-vertex point
articles.statement: If `(c, h)` is not a walk vertex, no horizontal step starts at `x = c` on height `h`.

articles.title: No vertical step through a non-vertex point
articles.statement:
A vertical step through the point `(c, h)` has `(c, h)` as a vertex; if `(c, h)` is not a walk
 vertex, no vertical step straddles height `h` on the line `x = c`.

articles.title: $k + 2 \ne k$ in $\mathrm{Fin}\, n$ for $n \ge 3$
articles.statement: In `Fin n` with `n ≥ 3`, `k + 2 ≠ k`.

articles.title: An odd number of vertical steps flips the ray parity
articles.statement: An odd number of vertical steps between cells `(a, b)` and `(a + 1, b)` flips the ray parity.

articles.title: Ray parity across a vertical segment counts separating steps
articles.statement:
The ray parities of cells `(a, b)` and `(a + 1, b)` add up to the number of separating vertical
 steps mod `2`.

articles.title: An odd number of horizontal steps flips the ray parity
articles.statement:
An odd number of horizontal steps between cells `(a, b)` and `(a, b + 1)` flips the ray
 parity.

articles.title: Vertical steps separating two horizontal neighbour cells
articles.statement:
The vertical steps of the walk on the segment `{a + 1} × [b, b + 1]` separating the cells `(a,
 b)` and `(a + 1, b)`.

articles.title: Parity of upward crossings across a vertical segment
articles.statement:
The upward crossing counts of cells `(a, b)` and `(a + 1, b)` plus the number of steps between
 them is even.

articles.title: Upward crossings of vertically adjacent cells differ by separating steps
articles.statement:
The upward crossings from cell `(a, b)` are those from `(a, b + 1)` plus the horizontal steps
 between the two cells.

articles.title: Index of a vertical step above a walk vertex
articles.statement:
In a simple walk, a vertical step on the segment above the vertex `pos d m` is step `m` or step
 `m - 1`.

articles.title: Index of a vertical step below a walk vertex
articles.statement:
In a simple walk, a vertical step on the segment below the vertex `pos d m` is step `m` or step
 `m - 1`.

articles.title: A closed walk is not all west steps
articles.statement: A closed walk does not consist of west steps only.

articles.title: A west run from a highest vertex ends in a south step
articles.statement:
From a highest vertex where the walk turns west, it makes `J ≥ 1` west steps and then a south
 step.

articles.title: Position after a run of west steps
articles.statement:
After `j` consecutive west steps from vertex `M`, the walk is `j` units to the left of `M` at
 the same height.

articles.title: A step changes the x-coordinate by at most one
articles.statement: A step changes the `x`-coordinate by `0` or `±1`.

articles.title: A closed walk crosses a vertical line equally often left and right
articles.statement: A walk crosses the line `x = m + 1/2` to the right as often as to the left.

articles.title: Some north-then-west corner has its below-left cell inside
articles.statement:
A simple closed walk without right turns has a north-then-west corner `M` whose below-left cell
 `((pos d M).1 - 1, (pos d M).2 - 1)` has ray parity `1`.

articles.title: A simple closed walk traverses each horizontal segment at most once
articles.statement: A simple closed walk traverses each horizontal unit segment at most once.

articles.title: Steps on a horizontal unit segment join its endpoints
articles.statement: A step on the horizontal segment `[a, a + 1] × {b}` goes from one endpoint to the other.

articles.title: A west run covering the top row is a single top run
articles.statement: A west run from `M` whose vertices cover the top row is a single top run.

articles.title: Single west run covering the top row
articles.statement:
Every vertex of the walk at the height of `M` is reached from `M` by a run of consecutive west
 steps.

articles.title: A simple closed walk traverses each vertical segment at most once
articles.statement: A simple closed walk traverses each vertical unit segment at most once.

articles.title: Steps on a vertical unit segment join its endpoints
articles.statement: A step on the vertical segment `{a + 1} × [b, b + 1]` goes from one endpoint to the other.

articles.title: A north step into a highest vertex is followed by a west step
articles.statement:
In a closed walk without right turns, a north step arriving at a highest vertex is followed by a
 west step.

articles.title: No south step arrives at a highest vertex
articles.statement: No south step arrives at a vertex of maximal height.

articles.title: No north step leaves a highest vertex
articles.statement: No north step leaves a vertex of maximal height.

articles.title: Top row is contiguous when every top corner starts a single run
articles.statement: If every highest north-then-west corner starts a single top run, the top row is contiguous.

articles.title: A single top run makes the top row contiguous
articles.statement: If the top row is covered by a single west run from a highest vertex, it is contiguous.

articles.title: A west step on the top row is followed by west or south
articles.statement: A west step on the top row is followed by a west or a south step, and stays on the top row.

articles.title: A closed walk crosses each vertical line an even number of times
articles.statement: A closed walk crosses each vertical line `x = m + 1/2` an even number of times.

articles.title: Number of crossings of a vertical line
articles.statement: The number of horizontal steps of the walk crossing the vertical line `x = m + 1/2`.

articles.title: Corner count of the interior counts inside cells around a point
articles.statement:
The corner count of the interior at `(vx, vy)` counts the inside cells among the four cells
 around that point.

articles.title: Even corner counts have zero corner weight
articles.statement: An even corner count has weight `0`.

articles.title: Corner weight at a left turn into the east direction
articles.statement:
At a left turn made of a south step followed by an east step, the corner weight of the interior
 is `1` if the cell to the left of the walk is inside and `-1` otherwise.

articles.title: Corner weight at a left turn into the north direction
articles.statement:
At a left turn made of an east step followed by a north step, the corner weight of the interior
 is `1` if the cell to the left of the walk is inside and `-1` otherwise.

articles.title: Corner weight at a left turn into the south direction
articles.statement:
At a left turn made of a west step followed by a south step, the corner weight of the interior
 is `1` if the cell to the left of the walk is inside and `-1` otherwise.

articles.title: Corner weight at a left turn into the west direction
articles.statement:
At a left turn made of a north step followed by a west step, the corner weight of the interior
 is `1` if the cell to the left of the walk is inside and `-1` otherwise.

articles.title: Zero corner weight where the walk continues horizontally
articles.statement: A vertex where the walk continues horizontally has weight `0`.

articles.title: Zero corner weight where the walk continues vertically
articles.statement: A vertex where the walk continues vertically has weight `0`.

articles.title: Straight steps of a simple closed walk carry no corner weight
articles.statement: A vertex where a simple closed walk goes straight has corner weight `0` for the interior.

articles.title: An inside cell lies below a horizontal step
articles.statement: An inside cell lies directly below some horizontal step of the walk.

articles.title: Finite set of interior cells of a closed walk
articles.statement:
The finite set of cells inside a closed walk (ray parity `1`). See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.WalkCellRegion.interiorCells`, the bounded face of the walk; the two agree for
 simple walks without right turns (`StatMech.Onsager.UmlaufsatzFinal.interiorCells_bridge`).

articles.title: Finiteness of the interior of a closed walk
articles.statement: A closed walk has finitely many inside cells.

articles.title: Interior cells by the even-odd rule
articles.statement: The cells inside the walk by the even-odd rule: those with ray parity `1`.

articles.title: A vertical direction is not horizontal
articles.statement: A vertical direction is not horizontal.

articles.title: A horizontal direction is not vertical
articles.statement: A horizontal direction is not vertical.

articles.title: Ray parity is constant around a non-vertex point
articles.statement:
At a lattice point that is not a vertex of the walk, the four cells around it have the same ray
 parity.

articles.title: Cells below a walk are outside
articles.statement: Cells below the walk are outside.

articles.title: Horizontal neighbours of different parity are separated by a vertical step
articles.statement:
If cells `(a, b)` and `(a + 1, b)` have different ray parities, a vertical step separates
 them.

articles.title: Minimal height of a walk
articles.statement: The minimal height of a vertex of the walk.

articles.title: Maximal height of a walk
articles.statement: The maximal height of a vertex of the walk.

articles.title: Face-graph adjacency as absence of a walk step between cells
articles.statement:
Adjacency in the face graph of the walk is the absence of a walk step on the common side of two
 cells.

articles.title: Ray-parity interior equals the bounded face components
articles.statement: The ray-parity interior of the walk coincides with the union of bounded face components.

articles.title: Four left turns from a pinch-free interior of Euler characteristic 1
articles.statement:
A simple closed walk without right turns whose interior is pinch-free with Euler characteristic
 `1` has four left turns.

articles.title: Corner defect of the interior is the number of left turns up to sign
articles.statement:
The corner defect of the interior equals `±cc d`, the sign given by the orientation of the
 walk.

articles.title: Corner defect of the interior as a sum over walk vertices
articles.statement:
For a simple closed walk, the corner defect of the interior is the sum of the corner weights at
 the walk vertices.

articles.title: Corner weights at the turns of a walk without right turns
articles.statement:
The corner weight of the interior at the vertex after step `i` is `±1` (sign given by the
 orientation) at a left turn and `0` at a straight step.

articles.title: Zero corner weight of the interior off the walk
articles.statement: A lattice point off the walk has corner weight `0` for the interior.

articles.title: A cycle graph has one connected component
articles.statement:
A cycle graph has one connected component. A specialization of
 `SimpleGraph.Preconnected.subsingleton_connectedComponent`.

articles.title: Number of edges of a cycle graph
articles.statement: The cycle graph on `m + 3` vertices has `m + 3` edges.

articles.title: Cycle graph has cycle rank one
articles.statement: The cycle graph has nullity (cycle rank) `1`.

articles.title: Vertical neighbours of different parity are separated by a horizontal step
articles.statement:
If cells `(a, b)` and `(a, b + 1)` have different ray parities, a horizontal step separates
 them.

articles.title: Pinch count of the ray-parity interior is zero
articles.statement:
The interior of a simple closed walk has pinch count `0`. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.WalkCellLocal.pinchCount_interiorCells_eq_zero`.

articles.title: Interior of a simple closed walk has no pinch points
articles.statement: The interior of a simple closed walk has no pinch points.

articles.title: Vertices of a simple walk are distinct sites
articles.statement: The vertices of a simple walk are distinct sites.

articles.title: Vertex of a walk as a lattice site
articles.statement: The `i`-th vertex of the walk as a site of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: Each lattice step has $\ell^1$-length one
articles.statement: Each step has `ℓ¹`-length `1`.

articles.title: Consecutive walk vertices are adjacent in the square lattice
articles.statement: Consecutive vertices of the walk are adjacent in the square lattice.

articles.title: Lattice Jordan curve theorem for simple closed walks
articles.statement:
Lattice Jordan curve theorem for a simple closed walk: its complement in the face graph of `ℤ²`
 has exactly one bounded connected component.

articles.title: Subgraph of a simple closed lattice walk has cycle rank one
articles.statement: The planar subgraph of a simple closed walk has nullity `1`.
