articles.title: Simple closed walk as an embedded cycle graph
articles.statement:
A simple closed walk as a planar subgraph of `ℤ²`: the cycle graph `cycleGraph (m + 3)` embedded
 by its vertex positions.

articles.title: Unit cell as a face of the square lattice
articles.statement:
The unit cell with lower-left corner `p`, viewed as a face of the square lattice, i.e. as the
 site `![p.1, p.2]` of the dual lattice.

articles.title: The inner component has finitely many cells
articles.statement: There are finitely many such cells.

articles.title: Cells of the inner face component
articles.statement: The cells whose faces lie in `innerComponent`.

articles.title: Neighbours in the image graph are walk predecessor and successor
articles.statement:
In the image graph of a simple closed walk, the neighbours of a vertex are its predecessor and
 successor on the walk.

articles.title: The inner face component is finite
articles.statement: The component `innerComponent` is bounded.

articles.title: Inner component of the face graph
articles.statement: The connected component of the face graph containing `lexInteriorFace`.

articles.title: Cells of the bounded face of a simple closed walk
articles.statement:
The cells of the bounded face of a simple closed walk without right turns. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.InteriorCells.interiorCells`, the ray-parity interior; they agree by
 `mem_interiorCells_iff_rayParity`.

articles.title: The face below the inside top corner is inside
articles.statement: The face `lexInteriorFace` is inside the walk.

articles.title: Face below-left of the inside top corner
articles.statement: The face of the cell below-left of the corner `lexInteriorIndex`.

articles.title: Defining property of the inside top corner
articles.statement: The defining property of `lexInteriorIndex`.

articles.title: Top corner with an inside cell below it
articles.statement:
A vertex `M` at which the walk turns from north to west and whose below-left cell is inside
 (chosen from `StatMech.Onsager.InsideConnected.lexmax_corner_cell_inside`).

articles.title: Membership in the bounded face
articles.statement: Membership in the bounded face.

articles.title: A face far outside the walk has ray parity zero
articles.statement: A face far outside the bounding box of the walk has ray parity `0`.

articles.title: Horizontally face-adjacent cells have the same ray parity
articles.statement: Horizontally adjacent cells joined in the face graph have the same ray parity.

articles.title: Vertically face-adjacent cells have the same ray parity
articles.statement: Vertically adjacent cells joined in the face graph have the same ray parity.

articles.title: Face-adjacent cells have the same ray parity
articles.statement: Cells adjacent in the face graph have the same ray parity.

articles.title: Ray parity is constant on face-graph components
articles.statement: Ray parity is constant on connected components of the face graph.

articles.title: Each walk step is an edge of the image graph
articles.statement: Each step of the walk is an edge of its image graph.

articles.title: Simple closed walk as a planar subgraph
articles.statement: A simple closed walk as a planar subgraph of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: Face graph of a closed walk
articles.statement:
The face graph of the walk: adjacent faces of the square lattice whose common side is not an
 edge of the walk.

articles.title: Corner count of the bounded face at a walk vertex
articles.statement:
At the vertex after step `k`, the bounded face has one cell after a left turn and two after a
 straight step.

articles.title: Corner count as a sum of four indicators
articles.statement:
The corner count at `v` as a sum of four indicators. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.CellEuler.cornerCount_eq_inter`.

articles.title: Zero corner weight of the bounded face off the walk
articles.statement: Points off the walk have corner weight `0` for the bounded face.

articles.title: Vertices of a walk's image graph are adjacent only to walk neighbours
articles.statement: In the image graph of a simple closed walk, a vertex is adjacent only to its walk neighbours.

articles.title: Consecutive left cells on a straight step are face-adjacent
articles.statement: Going straight, consecutive left cells are adjacent in the face graph of the walk.

articles.title: Every left cell lies in the bounded face
articles.statement: Every left cell of a simple closed walk without right turns lies in the bounded face.

articles.title: All left cells have the same ray parity
articles.statement: All left cells of a simple closed walk without right turns have the same ray parity.

articles.title: Every left cell has ray parity one
articles.statement: Every left cell of a simple closed walk without right turns is inside.

articles.title: Consecutive left cells have the same ray parity
articles.statement: Consecutive left cells of a simple closed walk without right turns have the same ray parity.

articles.title: Cell to the left of a walk step
articles.statement:
The cell to the left of step `k` of the walk. See also `StatMech.Onsager.Orientation.leftCell`;
 they agree by `StatMech.Onsager.UmlaufsatzFinal.leftCell_bridge`.

articles.title: Left and right cells of a step share that step
articles.statement: The left and right cells of a step are adjacent faces sharing that step.

articles.title: Lattice Jordan curve theorem, even-odd form
articles.statement:
Lattice Jordan curve theorem, even-odd form: a cell lies in the bounded face of a simple closed
 walk without right turns iff its ray parity is `1`.

articles.title: Bounded face of a simple closed walk has no pinch points
articles.statement: The bounded face of the walk has no pinch points.

articles.title: Face-graph component of an interior cell
articles.statement: The connected component of the walk's face graph containing an interior cell.

articles.title: Pinch count of the bounded face is zero
articles.statement:
The bounded face of the walk has pinch count `0`. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.PinchFree.pinchCount_eq_zero`.

articles.title: Three walk edges cannot meet at a vertex
articles.statement: Three walk edges cannot meet at one vertex of a simple closed walk.

articles.title: No right cell lies in the bounded face
articles.statement: No right cell of a simple closed walk without right turns lies in the bounded face.

articles.title: Cell to the right of a walk step
articles.statement: The cell to the right of step `k` of the walk.

articles.title: A side between interior and exterior cells is a walk edge
articles.statement: A side shared by an interior and an exterior cell is an edge of the walk.

articles.title: Cells on either side of a step lie in different faces
articles.statement: The two cells on either side of a walk step are in different face components.

articles.title: Vertex count of the skeleton
articles.statement: The skeleton has `(regVerts S).card` vertices.

articles.title: Number of cells is at most the nullity of the skeleton
articles.statement: The number of cells is at most the nullity of the skeleton.

articles.title: Adjacent cells have connected lower-left corners
articles.statement: The lower-left corners of two adjacent cells of `S` are connected in the skeleton.

articles.title: Edges of the skeleton are the edges of the cell complex
articles.statement: The edges of `cellSkeleton S` are the edges of the cell complex `S`.

articles.title: 1-skeleton of a cell complex as a planar subgraph
articles.statement: The 1-skeleton of `S` as a planar subgraph of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: 1-skeleton of a cell complex
articles.statement:
The 1-skeleton of the cell complex `S`: vertices are the corners of cells, edges the sides of
 cells.

articles.title: Corner defect of the bounded face equals the number of left turns
articles.statement:
The corner defect of the bounded face of a simple closed walk without right turns equals its
 number of left turns.

articles.title: Cell corners are connected to the lower-left corner
articles.statement: Every corner of a cell is connected in the skeleton to its lower-left corner.

articles.title: Corner weight of the bounded face at a walk vertex
articles.statement:
The corner weight of the bounded face at the vertex after step `k` is `1` after a left turn and
 `0` after a straight step.

articles.title: Euler characteristic at most 1 for a connected skeleton
articles.statement:
If the 1-skeleton of `S` is connected, then `eulerChar S ≤ 1`. See also
 `StatMech.Onsager.CellEulerBound.eulerChar_le_one`.

articles.title: Distinct cells form distinct bounded faces
articles.statement: Distinct cells form distinct bounded faces.

articles.title: Bounded face formed by a cell
articles.statement: The bounded face of the skeleton formed by a cell of `S`.

articles.title: The face component of a cell is bounded
articles.statement: The face component of a cell of `S` is bounded.

articles.title: Face component containing a cell
articles.statement: The face component of the skeleton containing the cell `c`.

articles.title: The face of a cell is enclosed on all four sides
articles.statement: The face of a cell of `S` is enclosed by the skeleton on all four sides.

articles.title: The face of a cell is alone in its component
articles.statement: The face of a cell of `S` is alone in its face component.

articles.title: Cell complex edges lie in the embedded skeleton
articles.statement: An edge of the cell complex is an edge of the embedded skeleton.

articles.title: Shared side of a cell and an adjacent face is an edge
articles.statement: The side shared by a cell of `S` and an adjacent face is an edge of `S`.

articles.title: Lower-left corner of a cell as a skeleton vertex
articles.statement: The lower-left corner of a cell of `S`, as a vertex of the skeleton.

articles.title: Corner of a cell as a skeleton vertex
articles.statement: A corner of a cell of `S`, as a vertex of the skeleton.

articles.title: Discrete Umlaufsatz for walks of length at least three
articles.statement: The discrete Umlaufsatz for walks of length at least `3` without right turns.

articles.title: Discrete Umlaufsatz for lattice walks without right turns
articles.statement:
Discrete Umlaufsatz (theorem of turning tangents) for lattice walks without right turns: a
 simple closed walk on `ℤ²` whose every turn is straight or a left quarter turn has exactly four
 left turns, i.e. its direction makes one full counterclockwise revolution. Right turns and
 reversals are excluded by hypothesis, so the walks covered are exactly counterclockwise
 boundaries of lattice rectangles (no reflex corner); the general signed statement is
 `StatMech.Onsager.GeneralUmlaufsatz.turnSum_eq_four_or_neg_four`. Compare H. Hopf, *Über die
 Drehung der Tangenten und Sehnen ebener Kurven*, Compositio Math. 2 (1935), for smooth curves.

articles.title: Discrete Umlaufsatz for walks of length at least three, shifted form
articles.statement: The discrete Umlaufsatz for walks of length `m + 3` without right turns.

articles.title: Interior of a simple closed walk has Euler characteristic at most 1
articles.statement:
The interior of a simple closed walk without right turns has Euler characteristic at most
 `1`.

articles.title: A simple closed walk without right turns has under eight left turns
articles.statement:
The hypothesis of `StatMech.Onsager.BaseCase.base_cc_eq_four` holds: a simple closed walk
 without right turns has fewer than eight left turns.

articles.title: Connectedness of the skeleton of the interior
articles.statement: The skeleton of the interior of a simple closed walk without right turns is connected.

articles.title: Ray-parity interior equals the bounded face
articles.statement: The ray-parity interior of a simple closed walk without right turns equals its bounded face.

articles.title: Interior cells have connected lower-left corners
articles.statement:
Any two interior cells of a simple closed walk without right turns have skeleton-connected
 lower-left corners.

articles.title: Agreement of the two definitions of the left cell
articles.statement: The two descriptions of the cell to the left of a step agree.

articles.title: A walk without right turns is positively oriented
articles.statement: The cell to the left of the first step is inside: the walk is positively oriented.

articles.title: A closed walk without right turns has length at least three
articles.statement: A closed walk without right turns or reversals has length at least `3`.

articles.title: Hopf's Umlaufsatz
articles.statement:
**Hopf's Umlaufsatz** for lattice polygons. A simple closed walk in `ℤ²` with at least three
steps and no U-turns has total turning `±4` quarter turns, that is rotation index `±1` (H. Hopf,
*Über die Drehung der Tangenten und Sehnen ebener Kurven*, 1935).

articles.title: Crossing points of the regular drawing of the complete bipartite graph
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a
natural number. In the regular drawing of $K_{n,n}$ in $\mathbb{Q}^2$, the left vertices are the
points $(0, i)$ and the right vertices are the points $(1, j)$ for $0 \le i, j < n$, and each edge
is the straight segment from $(0, i)$ to $(1, j)$. For $i < i'$ and $j' < j$, the edges from
$(0, i)$ to $(1, j)$ and from $(0, i')$ to $(1, j')$ cross at the point $(x, i + x(j - i))$, where
$x = (i' - i)/((i' - i) + (j - j'))$. The number of distinct points obtained in this way, over all
$i, i', j, j' < n$ with $i < i'$ and $j' < j$, equals $S_1 - S_2$, where $S_1$ is the sum of
$(n - a)(n - b)$ over all ordered pairs $(a, b)$ of coprime integers with $1 \le a, b \le n - 1$,
and $S_2$ is the sum of $(n - 2a)(n - 2b)$ over all ordered pairs $(a, b)$ of coprime integers
with $1 \le 2a \le n - 1$ and $1 \le 2b \le n - 1$.

The difference is taken in $\mathbb{N}$; since $S_2 \le S_1$, it is the ordinary difference.

## Sources

- Stéphane Legendre, "The Number of Crossings in a Regular Drawing of the Complete Bipartite Graph", Journal of Integer Sequences 12 (2009), Article 09.5.5, Proposition `count_all`, line 263, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL12/Legendre/legendre2.tex>.

articles.title: Quarter-turn rotation of unordered site pairs
articles.statement:
The bijection on unordered pairs of sites induced by the quarter-turn rotation
`(a, b) ↦ (-b, a)`. It maps lattice edges to lattice edges, but not to the dual edge crossing them:
`{(0,0), (1,0)}` goes to `{(0,0), (0,1)}`. For the geometric crossing use `sharedPrimalEdge`.

articles.title: Bijection between primal and dual edges
articles.statement: The bijection between primal and dual edges induced by `rot90Iso`.

articles.title: Rotated dual configuration
articles.statement:
The configuration in which `e` is open exactly when the inverse quarter turn `crossEdge.symm e`
of `e` is closed in `ω`. This is the dual configuration only up to the rotation: applying it twice
gives the half-turn of `ω` (`dualConfig_dualConfig`), not `ω`.

articles.title: Dual square lattice
articles.statement:
The dual square lattice. Its vertices are the face centres of `ℤ²`, relabelled as integer
points, so as a graph it is `hypercubicLattice 2`.

articles.title: Quarter-turn rotation as a permutation
articles.statement: The quarter-turn rotation as a permutation of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: Quarter-turn rotation of the square lattice
articles.statement: The quarter-turn rotation `(a, b) ↦ (-b, a)` of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: Inverse quarter-turn rotation
articles.statement: The inverse quarter-turn rotation `(a, b) ↦ (b, -a)` of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: Quarter-turn rotation as a lattice automorphism
articles.statement: The quarter-turn rotation as a graph automorphism of the square lattice.

articles.title: Rotational self-duality of the square lattice
articles.statement: The isomorphism between the square lattice and its dual given by the quarter-turn rotation.

articles.title: Identity self-duality of the square lattice
articles.statement: The identity isomorphism between the square lattice and its dual.

articles.title: Unordered pairs under an equivalence
articles.statement: An equivalence `α ≃ β` induces an equivalence of unordered pairs `Sym2 α ≃ Sym2 β`.

articles.title: Straight-line planar graph
articles.statement:
A simple graph $G$ with vertex set $V$ is straight-line
planar if either $V$ is empty or there is an injective map $f$ from $V$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$
such that, for any two different edges $vw$ and $xy$ of $G$, the closed segment from $f(v)$
to $f(w)$ and the closed segment from $f(x)$ to $f(y)$ meet only in points of
$\{f(v), f(w)\} \cap \{f(x), f(y)\}$.

articles.title: Closed segment in the plane
articles.statement:
For points $a$ and $b$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$, the closed segment
from $a$ to $b$ is the set of points $a + t(b - a)$ with $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $0 \le t \le 1$.

articles.title: Csóka–Lo–Norin–Wu–Yepremyan theorem on 2-regular minors
articles.statement:
For every natural number $t$,
every finite simple graph $G$ whose average degree (the sum of the vertex degrees divided by the
number of vertices, taken to be $0$ when $G$ has no vertices) is at least $4t/3 - 2$ contains
every 2-regular simple graph $H$ on $t$ vertices as a minor: there are nonempty, pairwise
disjoint sets of vertices of $G$, one for each vertex of $H$, each inducing a connected subgraph
of $G$, such that whenever two vertices of $H$ are adjacent, some edge of $G$ joins their sets.

Csoka, Lo, Norin, Wu and Yepremyan proved this, verifying a conjecture of Reed and Wood; the
non-strict threshold follows from the form of their bound in Corollary 8 and Lemma 9.

## Sources

- Endre Csoka, Irene Lo, Sergey Norin, Hehui Wu and Liana Yepremyan, The extremal function for disconnected minors, Journal of Combinatorial Theory Series B (2017), arXiv:1509.01185, https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01185.

articles.title: Average-degree conjecture for 2-regular minors
articles.statement:
For every natural number $t$, every
finite simple graph whose average degree is at least $4t/3 - 2$ (the average degree of the graph
with no vertices being taken as $0$) contains every 2-regular simple graph on $t$ vertices as a
minor.

articles.title: Minor via branch sets
articles.statement:
For finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, $G$ has $H$ as a minor if
there is a family of vertex sets $B_w$ of $G$, one for each vertex $w$ of $H$, such that each
$B_w$ is nonempty and induces a connected subgraph of $G$, the sets $B_u$ and $B_v$ are disjoint
whenever $u \ne v$, and for every edge $uv$ of $H$ some vertex of $B_u$ is adjacent in $G$ to
some vertex of $B_v$.

articles.title: Planar graphs have subquadratic universal point sets
articles.statement:
There is a function
$f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $f(n)/n^2 \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n$
some finite set $P$ of at most $f(n)$ points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a universal point set for
$n$-vertex planar graphs: every straight-line planar simple graph on the vertex set
$\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has a crossing-free straight-line embedding with all its vertices in $P$.

Taylor Gordon (Theorem 1 of the cited preprint) constructs universal point sets of size
$n \exp(O(\sqrt{\log n}))$ for $n$-vertex planar graphs, using small superpatterns and the
reduction of Bannister, Cheng, Devanny and Eppstein.

## Sources

- Taylor Gordon, Almost Linear Universal Point Sets for Planar Graphs, arXiv preprint (2026), arXiv:2609.10916, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10916; Michael J. Bannister, Zhanpeng Cheng, William E. Devanny and David Eppstein, Superpatterns and Universal Point Sets, arXiv:1308.0403, https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0403.

articles.title: Subquadratic universal point sets
articles.statement:
The statement that there is a function
$f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $f(n)/n^2 \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n$
some finite set of at most $f(n)$ points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a universal point set for
$n$-vertex planar graphs.

articles.title: Straight-line planar embedding
articles.statement:
A map $p$ from the vertex set of a simple graph $G$ to
$\mathbb{R}^2$ is a crossing-free straight-line embedding of $G$ if $p$ is injective, the closed
segments $[p(u), p(v)]$ and $[p(x), p(y)]$ of any two different edges $uv$ and $xy$ meet only in
points $p(z)$ with $z$ an endpoint of both edges, and no vertex $w$ other than $u$ and $v$ has
$p(w)$ on the segment $[p(u), p(v)]$ of an edge $uv$.

articles.title: Universal point set for planar graphs
articles.statement:
A finite set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is
universal for $n$-vertex planar graphs if every straight-line planar simple graph $G$ on the
vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has a crossing-free straight-line embedding $p$ with $p(v) \in P$
for every vertex $v$.

articles.title: Closed contour as an even-degree edge set
articles.statement: Every site has even degree in the edge set `E`.

articles.title: Degree of a site in an edge set
articles.statement: The number of edges of `E` at the site `v`.

articles.title: Edge flip relation of an edge set
articles.statement: The flip relation of `E`: the primal edge between the faces `a` and `b` is in `E`.

articles.title: Number of horizontal contour edges below a height
articles.statement: The number of horizontal edges of `E` below height `b` in the column `[c, c + 1]`.

articles.title: Horizontal edges below a face in its column
articles.statement: The horizontal edges in the column `[a, a + 1]` at heights at most `b`.

articles.title: Parity coloring changes across vertical contour edges
articles.statement:
For every closed contour `E`, the parity coloring changes between horizontally adjacent faces
exactly when the vertical edge between them is in `E`.

articles.title: Four nearest neighbours of a site
articles.statement: The four nearest neighbours of `v`: right, left, up, down.

articles.title: Parity coloring of faces by an edge set
articles.statement:
The parity coloring of faces: `f` is colored when an odd number of horizontal edges of `E`
lie directly below it in its column.

articles.title: Even-degree image of a planar lattice subgraph
articles.statement: Every site has even degree in the image of `P`.

articles.title: Faithful discrete Jordan property for even-degree subgraphs
articles.statement: Every `PlanarZ2Subgraph` with all degrees even satisfies `whc_FaithfulDiscreteJordan`.

articles.title: Induced subgraphs of locally finite graphs are locally finite
articles.statement: An induced subgraph of a locally finite graph is locally finite.

articles.title: Two odd-degree vertices lie in one component
articles.statement:
In a locally finite graph with finite support, two vertices of odd degree whose other
vertices all have even degree lie in the same component (the handshake lemma applied to a
component).

articles.title: Spanning subgraph formed by a path
articles.statement: The spanning subgraph formed by a path from `y` to `x` in `K`.

articles.title: Whitney duality in the bridge direction
articles.statement:
Whitney's duality in the bridge direction for `P`: for every subgraph `K` of `P` and edge
`xy` of `P` not in `K` with dual edge `f0g0`, if `x` and `y` are disconnected in `K`, then
`f0` and `g0` are connected in the face-region graph of `K` with `f0g0` deleted.

articles.title: Closed face walk around a lattice vertex
articles.statement: The closed walk through the four faces having the site `(c, d)` as a corner.

articles.title: Cut-flip count along a walk
articles.statement:
The number of cut flips of `H` and `f0g0` along `w`; equal to
`wcl_flipCount (wcl_cutFlip H f0 g0) w`.

articles.title: Chosen lattice walk between two faces
articles.statement: A fixed lattice walk from `o` to `f`, chosen using connectedness of `ℤ²`.

articles.title: Even-flip condition on closed lattice walks
articles.statement: Every closed lattice walk has an even number of flips.

articles.title: Cut coloring separating the ends of a dual edge
articles.statement:
For every graph `H` of `ℤ²` and dual edge `f0g0` such that the cut flip relation has even
loops, there is a cut coloring distinguishing `f0` from `g0`, and `f0`, `g0` are disconnected
in the face-region graph of `H` with `f0g0` deleted.

articles.title: Cut flip relation of a lattice graph and a dual edge
articles.statement: The cut flip relation: steps across a dual edge of `H` or across the extra dual edge `f0g0`.

articles.title: Number of flips along a lattice walk
articles.statement: The number of steps of the walk `w` that are flips (in either direction).

articles.title: Closed walk around a unit square
articles.statement: The closed walk around the unit square with corners `(0, 0)` and `(1, -1)`.

articles.title: Symmetry of a flip relation on lattice edges
articles.statement: The flip relation is symmetric on lattice edges.

articles.title: Face coloring by parity of flips
articles.statement: The face coloring given by the parity of the number of flips along the chosen walk from `o`.

articles.title: Whitney's cut–cycle duality
articles.statement:
**Whitney's cut–cycle duality** for subgraphs of `ℤ²` (H. Whitney, *Planar graphs*, 1933):
for every `H` and lattice edge `pq` not in `H`, with `fg` the dual edge across `pq`, the
endpoints `p` and `q` are connected in `H` iff `f` and `g` are disconnected in the
face-region graph of `H` with `fg` deleted.

articles.title: Face-region graph of a square-lattice subgraph
articles.statement:
The face-region graph of `G`: two adjacent faces of `ℤ²` are joined unless the primal edge
between them (`sharedPrimalEdge`) is an edge of `G`. This is the faithful planar dual
complement of `G`.

articles.title: Face coloring compatible with a subgraph
articles.statement: `φ` changes value exactly across the dual edges of `H`.

articles.title: Cut coloring of a subgraph with an extra dual edge
articles.statement: `φ` changes value exactly across the dual edges of `H` and the extra dual edge `f0g0`.

articles.title: Number of edge crossings of a face walk
articles.statement: The number of steps of the face walk `w` across an edge of `H`.

articles.title: Faithful discrete Jordan statement for the face count
articles.statement:
The face count of a finite subgraph of `ℤ²`: the bounded components of its face-region graph
are equinumerous with `Fin (nullity P.G)`, so the number of bounded faces is the cycle rank. Only
the number of faces is asserted, not which cycle bounds which face.

articles.title: Number of bounded faces of a lattice subgraph
articles.statement: The number of finite components of the face-region graph of `P`: the bounded faces of `P`.

articles.title: Unit square with its bottom edge removed
articles.statement: The unit square with its bottom edge removed.

articles.title: Primal edge between two faces lies in a subgraph
articles.statement: The primal edge between the faces `a` and `b` is an edge of `H`.

articles.title: Face coloring supported at a single face
articles.statement: The face coloring that is true only at the face `(0, 0)`.

articles.title: Chromatic minus cochromatic number of a random graph tends to infinity
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $C$, the probability that a uniformly random simple graph $G$ on the vertex set
$\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ (that is, $G \sim G(n, 1/2)$) satisfies $\chi(G) - \zeta(G) > C$
tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\chi$ is the chromatic number and $\zeta$ the
cochromatic number.

Petkov and GPT-5.6 improved Heckel's bounds to $\chi(G) - \zeta(G) \gg n / (\log n)^3$ with
high probability for $G \sim G(n, 1/2)$, as Heckel predicted; this answers Erdős Problem 625 in
the affirmative.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problem #625, erdosproblems.com (live page, LaTeX source and forum threads read 2026-10-22), https://www.erdosproblems.com/625; S. Petkov (with GPT-5.6), proof for Erdős Problem #625, https://github.com/SamPetkov/Erdos/blob/main/625/arxiv_625.pdf.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 625
articles.statement:
The statement that for every natural number $C$, the probability
that a uniformly random simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ (that is,
$G \sim G(n, 1/2)$) satisfies $\chi(G) - \zeta(G) > C$ tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$, where
$\chi$ is the chromatic number and $\zeta$ the cochromatic number. In other words,
$\chi(G) - \zeta(G) \to \infty$ with high probability.

articles.title: Probability of a large chromatic–cochromatic gap
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $C$ and $n$, the
proportion of simple graphs $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with
$\chi(G) - \zeta(G) > C$, where $\chi$ is the chromatic number and $\zeta$ the cochromatic
number; equivalently, the probability of this event for a uniformly random labelled graph,
$G \sim G(n, 1/2)$.

articles.title: Connectivity threshold for random $k$-out friendship graphs
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $N$,
let $P_{kN}$ be the proportion of the assignments giving each of $N$ people exactly $k$ friends
other than themselves that connect all $N$ people. Then $P_{kN} \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$ for
every $k \ge 2$, and $P_{1N} \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$.

Friendship need not be symmetric: two people are joined when either one chose the other, so a
chain of friends is a path in the underlying undirected graph. Ulam asked for $P_{kN}$ and for
its limit as $N \to \infty$, $0$ or $1$.

## Sources

- S. Ulam, Problem 38 of the Scottish Book; the symmetric case was solved by Erdős for `k ≥ 2`, and D. S. Jungreis gave a detailed general solution; see the commentary in R. D. Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2015).

articles.title: Probability that a random $k$-out assignment connects everyone
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$
and $N$, $P_{kN}$ is the number of assignments that give each of $N$ people a set of exactly $k$
friends other than themselves and connect all $N$ people, divided by the number of all
assignments that give each person a set of exactly $k$ friends other than themselves. When there
is no such assignment, $P_{kN} = 0$.

articles.title: Assignments that connect everyone
articles.statement:
Let $c$ assign to each person $i$ among $N$ people a
set $c(i)$ of people, the friends of $i$. The assignment $c$ connects all $N$ people when, for
all people $a$ and $b$, there are $m \ge 0$ and people $p_0 = a, p_1, \dots, p_m = b$ such that
for each $j < m$, $p_j$ is a friend of $p_{j+1}$ or $p_{j+1}$ is a friend of $p_j$.

articles.title: Reachability by a chain of friends
articles.statement:
Let $c$ assign to each person $i$ among $N$ people a
set $c(i)$ of people, the friends of $i$. A person $b$ is reachable from a person $a$ if there are
$m \ge 0$ and people $p_0 = a, p_1, \dots, p_m = b$ such that for each $j < m$, $p_j$ is a friend
of $p_{j+1}$ or $p_{j+1}$ is a friend of $p_j$.

articles.title: Density of a graph in a graphon
articles.statement:
For a graph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ and
a function $W$ of two real variables, the density $d(H, W)$ is the sum of the labelled densities
$\tau(G, W)$ over all graphs $G$ on $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ that are isomorphic to $H$.

When $W$ is a graphon, $d(H, W)$ is the probability that the $W$-random graph on
$\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ is isomorphic to $H$.

articles.title: Lovász's finitely forcible optimum conjecture is false
articles.statement:
There are graphs $H_1, \dots, H_\ell$
and reals $d_1, \dots, d_\ell$ such that some graphon $W$ satisfies $d(H_i, W) = d_i$ for every $i$,
but no finitely forcible graphon $W_0$ satisfies $d(H_i, W_0) = d_i$ for every $i$.

Grzesik, Kráľ and Lovász (Theorem 18) construct such graphs and reals for which every graphon
$W$ with $d(H_i, W) = d_i$ for all $i$ is weakly isomorphic to a member of a family none of whose
graphons is finitely forcible.

## Sources

- L. Lovász (joint work with B. Szegedy), Extremal graphs and graph limits, in Graph Theory, Oberwolfach Reports 7 (2010), no. 11, pp. 554-555, question 1, DOI 10.4171/OWR/2010/11; resolution: A. Grzesik, D. Kráľ and L. M. Lovász, Elusive extremal graphs, Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. (3) 121 (2020), 1685-1736, DOI 10.1112/plms.12382, arXiv:1807.01141, Conjecture 1 (Lovász): if some convergent sequence of graphs has limit densities d(H_i) = d_i for i = 1, ..., ℓ, then some finitely forcible such sequence does; Theorem 18: there are a family W of graphons, graphs H_1, ..., H_ℓ and reals d_1, ..., d_ℓ such that a graphon is weakly isomorphic to a member of W if and only if d(H_i, W) = d_i for all i, and no graphon in W is finitely forcible; 'Our main result (Theorem 18) implies that the conjecture is false', https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.01141.

articles.title: Lovász's finitely forcible optimum conjecture
articles.statement:
The proposition that for all graphs
$H_1, \dots, H_\ell$ and reals $d_1, \dots, d_\ell$, if some graphon $W$ satisfies
$d(H_i, W) = d_i$ for every $i$, then some finitely forcible graphon $W_0$ satisfies
$d(H_i, W_0) = d_i$ for every $i$.

This is Lovász's conjecture that every extremal problem has a finitely forcible optimum
(Oberwolfach Report 11/2010, p. 554), in the form of Grzesik, Kráľ and Lovász, Conjecture 1.

articles.title: Finitely forcible graphon
articles.statement:
A function $W$ of two real variables is finitely forcible if
there are finitely many graphs $H_1, \dots, H_\ell$ such that every graphon $W'$ with
$d(H_i, W') = d(H_i, W)$ for all $i$ is weakly isomorphic to $W$.

articles.title: Graphon
articles.statement:
A graphon is a function $W$ of two real variables that is jointly measurable
(measurable as a function on $\mathbb{R}^2$), symmetric ($W(x, y) = W(y, x)$ for all real $x, y$)
and takes values in $[0, 1]$ at every point of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Only the values of $W$ on $[0, 1]^2$ enter the densities.

articles.title: Labelled density
articles.statement:
For a graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ and a function $W$
of two real variables, the labelled density of $G$ in $W$ is

$$\tau(G, W) = \int_{[0,1]^k} \prod_{i < j} w_{ij}(x) \, dx,$$

where the integral is with respect to Lebesgue measure (and is taken to be $0$ if the integrand is
not integrable), the product runs over the pairs $i < j$ of vertices, and $w_{ij}(x) = W(x_i, x_j)$
if $i$ and $j$ are adjacent in $G$ and $w_{ij}(x) = 1 - W(x_i, x_j)$ otherwise.

When $W$ is a graphon, $\tau(G, W)$ is the probability that the $W$-random graph on
$\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ (independent uniform points $x_i \in [0, 1]$, each pair $\{i, j\}$ joined
independently with probability $W(x_i, x_j)$) equals $G$.

articles.title: Weak isomorphism
articles.statement:
Two functions $W_1$ and $W_2$ of two real variables are weakly isomorphic
if $d(H, W_1) = d(H, W_2)$ for every natural number $k$ and every graph $H$ on the vertex set
$\{0, \dots, k-1\}$, where $d(H, W)$ is the density of $H$ in $W$.

The notion is meant for graphons, but no graphon condition is imposed on $W_1$ and $W_2$.

articles.title: The independence ratio of random regular graphs converges
articles.statement:
For every integer $d \ge 1$
there is a real number $c$ such that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, the probability that the
independence ratio $\alpha(G)/n$ of a uniformly random $d$-regular simple graph $G$ on the vertex
set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ differs from $c$ by more than $\varepsilon$ tends to $0$ as
$n \to \infty$. Here $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number of $G$, the largest size of an
independent set of vertices, and the probability is taken to be $0$ for the $n$ with no
$d$-regular simple graph on $n$ vertices.

## Sources

- M. Abért, Some questions (2010), Question 18 (B. Bollobás), https://www.renyi.hu/~abert/questions.pdf; resolution: M. Bayati, D. Gamarnik and P. Tetali, Combinatorial approach to the interpolation method and scaling limits in sparse random graphs, Ann. Probab. 41 (2013), no. 3, 1803-1826, DOI 10.1214/12-AOP816, arXiv:0912.2444, Theorem 3: for every r and every model of §2 (independent sets included, H(G) = size of a largest independent set) there is H(r) with lim N^{-1} H(G(N, r)) = H(r) w.h.p. (N along Nr even); §1: G(N, r) is chosen uniformly from the r-regular graphs on N nodes and the result resolves the question whether |I_N|/N converges in probability; §2: results proved w.h.p. for the configuration model carry over to simple regular graphs, https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.2444.

articles.title: Bollobás's question on the independence ratio of random regular graphs
articles.statement:
The statement
that for every integer $d \ge 1$ there is a real number $c$ such that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
the probability that the independence ratio $\alpha(G)/n$ of a uniformly random $d$-regular simple
graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ differs from $c$ by more than $\varepsilon$
tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$. Here $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number of $G$, the largest
size of an independent set of vertices, and the probability is taken to be $0$ for the $n$ with
no $d$-regular simple graph on $n$ vertices.

The question whether this holds is due to Bollobás and is Question 18 in Abért's list of problems.

articles.title: Proportion of regular graphs with nonsingular adjacency matrix
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $d$
and $n$, this is the real number obtained by dividing the number of $d$-regular simple graphs on
the vertex set $\{0, 1, \ldots, n-1\}$ whose adjacency matrix has nonzero determinant over
$\mathbb{Q}$ by the number of all $d$-regular simple graphs on that vertex set; it is $0$ when
there is no $d$-regular simple graph on that vertex set. It is the probability that the adjacency
matrix of the uniformly random $d$-regular graph $G(n, d)$ is nonsingular.

Nonsingularity over $\mathbb{Q}$ is the same as nonsingularity over $\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Deviation probability of the independence ratio of a random regular graph
articles.statement:
For natural
numbers $n$ and $d$ and real numbers $c$ and $\varepsilon$, the probability that the independence
ratio $\alpha(G)/n$ of a uniformly random $d$-regular simple graph $G$ on the vertex set
$\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ differs from $c$ by more than $\varepsilon$, where $\alpha(G)$ is the
independence number of $G$: the number of $d$-regular simple graphs $G$ on this vertex set with
$|\alpha(G)/n - c| > \varepsilon$ divided by the number of all $d$-regular simple graphs on it,
or $0$ when there is no $d$-regular simple graph on it. For $n = 0$ the ratio $\alpha(G)/n$ is
read as $0$.

articles.title: Nonsingularity of adjacency matrices of random regular graphs
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$d \ge 3$, the probability that the adjacency matrix of the uniformly random $d$-regular simple
graph on $n$ labeled vertices has nonzero determinant (over $\mathbb{Q}$, equivalently over
$\mathbb{R}$) tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$ along the natural numbers $n$ with $nd$ even.

Huang proved more: for every fixed $d \ge 3$ there is $c > 0$ such that the adjacency matrix of a
random $d$-regular directed or undirected graph on $n$ vertices is singular with probability at
most $n^{-c}$ for all large $n$, in the configuration model and, by contiguity, in the uniform
model.

## Sources

- V. Vu, problem (1) of the problem session, in Combinatorics, Oberwolfach Reports 11 (2014), Report 01/2014, pp. 84-85, DOI 10.4171/OWR/2014/01; resolution: J. Huang, Invertibility of adjacency matrices for random d-regular graphs, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 18, 3977-4032, DOI 10.1215/00127094-2021-0006, arXiv:1807.06465, Theorem 1.3: for fixed d ≥ 3, P(A is singular in R) ≤ n^(-c) for n sufficiently large (directed and undirected d-regular graphs); Section 1.1: by a contiguity argument the results hold for the uniform model, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06465.

articles.title: Vu's problem on nonsingular adjacency matrices of random regular graphs
articles.statement:
This is the
statement that for every natural number $d \ge 3$, the probability that the adjacency matrix of
the uniformly random $d$-regular simple graph on $n$ labeled vertices is nonsingular tends to $1$
as $n \to \infty$, where $n$ runs over the natural numbers with $nd$ even. Here the probability is
the proportion of the $d$-regular simple graphs on $\{0, 1, \ldots, n-1\}$ whose adjacency matrix
has nonzero determinant over $\mathbb{Q}$.

The restriction to $nd$ even is natural: $d$-regular graphs on $n$ vertices exist only for such
$n$.

articles.title: Regular simple graphs on a labelled vertex set
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $d$, the
finite set of all $d$-regular simple graphs on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$; the uniformly
random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices is uniform on this set. It is empty when $nd$ is odd or
$1 \le n \le d$.
